info.title: Angaza360 API
info.description:
Multi-tenant ERP for Kenyan MSMEs. Every tenant's data lives in its own PostgreSQL schema and is reached only through the authenticated session's tenant context.

**Money is never a JSON number.** On input, money is a decimal string (`"1250.00"`); on output it is a string of integer minor units — KES cents (`"125000"`). A JSON number in a money field is rejected by the validator.

**Quantities and tax rates are decimal strings too**, and are NOT money.

Authenticate with `POST /v1/auth/login`, then send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

bearerAuth.description: Access token from POST /v1/auth/login. Carries the user, role and tenant; the tenant schema is derived from it and never from a request field.

costPrice.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

price.description: VAT-EXCLUSIVE shelf price in cents; VAT, when charged, is added on top.

taxClass.description: A product's VAT status under the VAT Act 2013 (Task 3B.1). STANDARD_RATED charges the standard rate; ZERO_RATED is vatable at 0% (the seller may still recover input VAT); EXEMPT is outside VAT. Output VAT is charged ONLY by a VAT-registered tenant, and only on STANDARD_RATED lines.

kind.description: GOOD is stock (received, held, valued, depleted). SERVICE carries no stock: its sale posts revenue and VAT/TOT only — no stock movement and no cost of sales. Fixed once created.

stockCount.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

minStockThreshold.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

reorderQuantity.description: Decimal value as a string, or null.

avgCost.description: DERIVED cache of stockValue / stockCount, rounded to cents. Never an input to stockValue.

stockValue.description: AUTHORITATIVE carrying value in cents. Moves only by exact posted deltas; never recomputed as stockCount * avgCost.

debit.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

credit.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

unitCost.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

totalCost.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

balanceQty.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

balanceValue.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

avgCostAfter.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

avgCostAfterPrecise.description: The derived unit rate after this movement, in cents to six decimal places. A rate, not money.

goodsReceiptId.description: The goods receipt this movement was part of, when it came from a purchase order (Task 5.1). NULL on every other movement — an ad-hoc receipt, a sale, a transfer, an adjustment — which is the truthful statement that no PO was involved.

purchaseOrderLineId.description: The purchase-order line this movement fulfilled. Always paired with goodsReceiptId, or both are null.

type.description: MAIN (the single authoritative pool), POS (a till), ECOMMERCE (a storefront channel), BRANCH and ATTENDANT (the same model, enabled by adding rows — no schema change).

isDefault.description: Marks the single MAIN pool. Always the same row as type = MAIN.

isOfflineCapable.description: Whether this location may sell while disconnected. Never true for MAIN or ECOMMERCE.

leaseWindowMinutes.description: The admin-set lease window in minutes. NULL means FOREVER — this location's allocation never freezes. Set only on offline-capable locations. This is CONFIG: lease expiry and the freeze to PENDING_RECONCILIATION are enforced by the offline server task, not by anything reading this field today.

sessionStart.description: Optional daily selling window start, 24-hour "HH:MM". Set together with sessionEnd.

requestedQty.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

approvedQty.description: What the admin actually granted; may differ from requestedQty. NULL unless APPROVED.

decidedBy.description: Who took the request out of PENDING — the approver, the decliner, or (for a cancellation) the requester.

transferId.description: The TRANSFER_IN stock movement that delivered the approved stock into the requesting location. Set only on APPROVED; a DECLINED or CANCELLED request moves nothing and carries none.

quantity.description: What this location currently OWNS.

threshold.description: Product.minStockThreshold, the catalog's reorder point, applied per location slice. A threshold of zero raises no alert.

shortfall.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

reorderQuantity.description: Decimal value as a string, or null.

suggestedTransferQty.description: What to move to clear the alert: the catalog reorder quantity, but never less than the shortfall.

mainAvailable.description: What the MAIN pool owns, so the admin can see whether a top-up is possible.

openingFloat.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

closingFloat.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents), or null when not yet known.

expectedCash.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents), or null when not yet known.

variance.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents), or null when not yet known.

locationId.description: Where the shift was opened (M4.5 W3). Null on a shift opened before location assignment existed.

cashierAssigned.description: True when a cashier opened it under their location assignment: its sales must come from that location.

totAccrued.description: Turnover Tax accrued on this sale (Task 3B.2) — posted Dr 6110 / Cr 2110 inside the sale's entry for a TURNOVER_TAX tenant; 0 otherwise. A tax on the business: NOT part of what the customer pays.

sellingLocationId.description: The location this sale drew its stock from, and the location a void returns it to. NULL on sales recorded before the sale path became location-aware — those drew from MAIN by definition.

origin.description: ONLINE (rung at the server) or OFFLINE_SYNCED (captured on a device and replayed through the same atomic sale transaction).

businessTimestamp.description: When the sale ACTUALLY happened. The journal entry is dated to this. NULL on an online sale, where createdAt already is that instant.

syncedAt.description: When the capture arrived at the server. Never conflated with businessTimestamp.

idempotencyKey.description: The capturing device's key for this sale. Replaying it is a no-op. NULL on an online sale.

originalBusinessDate.description: Non-null ONLY when the closed-period fallback was taken: the capture's own period had already closed, so the entry posted into the current open period and the true business date is recorded here.

fiscalStatus.description: KRA eTIMS state. NOT_REQUESTED is the DEFAULT and the common case — most MSME sales are informal, carry no buyer PIN, and are validly finalized with no fiscal invoice. PENDING_ETIMS means a KRA invoice was asked for and is not signed yet (queued on a connectivity failure); SIGNED means KRA signed it; FAILED means KRA rejected it, or retries were exhausted. Signing never alters the sale's money, stock or ledger entries.

lineCogs.description: The exact cost this line posted to the ledger. NULL on sales recorded before Task 3.1-FIX.

amount.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

anyOf.description: How an MPESA tender's money came in: STK (a prompt pushed to the phone), TILL (Buy Goods) or PAYBILL.
Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

cashReceived.description: CASH: the physical cash handed over (cents); null when not recorded.

logoUrl.description: Present only when a logo is set AND showLogoOnReceipt is true.

rate.description: The rate applied under this code: the standard rate for B, "0.00" otherwise.

vatableAmount.description: Σ lineNet of the lines charged under this code.

vatAmount.description: Σ lineVat of those lines. Zero for every code but B.

taxCodeSummary.description: The VAT breakdown by KRA tax code, as on a Kenyan fiscal receipt. A non-VAT-registered seller's receipt carries a single D line — "No VAT — not VAT registered". Σ vatAmount == vatSummary.vatTotal, asserted when the receipt is built.

amount.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

amountTendered.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

changeDue.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

invoiceNumber.description: The device's sequential eTIMS invoice number, as a string.

rcptSign.description: KRA's receipt signature. Reproduced verbatim; never generated locally.

qrCode.description: KRA's verification URL, for the QR a buyer scans to check the invoice.

etims.description: The KRA fiscal block. Every artifact is null unless the sale was SIGNED — most sales are NOT_REQUESTED and were validly finalized without a fiscal invoice, and a receipt must never imply one was filed.

creditLimit.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

creditBalance.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

keyRef.description: Names WHICH key encrypted the blob (the Cloud KMS migration seam). Naming a key does not disclose it.

healthStatus.description: The last live verify against the provider (M4.5 W1): never run, accepted, or failing.

lastHealthError.description: The last verify failure in words. Never contains a secret.

IntegrationCredentialInput.description: Safe view of a stored integration credential. Secret fields are write-only: they are accepted on PUT and are never returned by any endpoint.

locationLeaseWindowMinutes.description: The LOCATION's admin-set lease policy, in minutes. NULL means FOREVER — a lease taken against it never expires.

status.description: Only an ACTIVE device may take custody and sell. A SUSPENDED or RETIRED device may still SYNC what it already captured — refusing would strand real sales.

leaseStartedAt.description: When this device last TOOK CUSTODY of its location's allocation.

leaseExpiresAt.description: leaseStartedAt + the location's window AT THE TIME CUSTODY WAS TAKEN. NULL means FOREVER and never expires. Editing the location's policy later does not move a live lease.

holdsCustody.description: true while a lease has been started and not ended. A device holding no custody cannot block a period close.

leaseExpired.description: true only when a NON-NULL expiry is in the past. A forever lease is never expired. An expired lease whose stock has been frozen reads false here, because the freeze ends the lease — the freeze row is where that state lives.

status.description: PENDING_RECONCILIATION (live — immobilised, awaiting the truth or a decision), RELEASED_BY_SYNC (the device synced; real sales posted and the remainder went back to MAIN), or WRITTEN_OFF (an admin posted the loss, Dr 5300 / Cr 1200).

leaseExpiredAt.description: The lease expiry that triggered this freeze.

productCount.description: How many product slices were immobilised when the freeze was taken.

resolvedBy.description: NULL on a sync release — nobody decided anything, the device simply reported what it sold. Always set on a write-off: an accounting loss names its decider.

outcome.description: POSTED (became a real Sale through the atomic sale transaction), REPLAYED (this key had already posted — a no-op, no second journal entry and no second stock decrement), or NEEDS_RESOLUTION (could not post; NOTHING was posted and the capture is queued for the owner).

businessTimestamp.description: When the sale actually happened — preserved exactly as captured.

entryDate.description: The date the journal entry was DATED to. Null when nothing posted.

postedToCurrentPeriod.description: true when the closed-period fallback was taken: this capture's own period had already closed, so the entry posted into the current open period instead of being dropped.

originalBusinessDate.description: The true business date, recorded on the sale when the fallback was taken.

fiscalStatus.description: The sale's resulting KRA fiscal status, or NOT_ATTEMPTED when eTIMS could not be tried (the tenant has not configured it).

etims.description: Present only for a capture that requested a KRA invoice (Task 4.1). A device cannot sign — eTIMS needs KRA — so the SERVER signs on sync, as a deferred online operation through the same signSaleInvoice the online POS uses. A signing failure NEVER changes the sale's outcome above: the sale is already committed and final.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

freezeResolution.description: Present only when this sync met an active lease freeze over the device's location.

payload.description: The exact captured payload that was attempted, as JSON, so the owner can see what the sale was. Money and quantities inside it are strings, as everywhere.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

totalCost.description: The carrying value written off for this product — the amount posted Dr 5300 / Cr 1200.

totalWrittenOff.description: Total posted to 5300 Inventory Write-offs by this write-off, in cents.

tin.description: The TENANT's own KRA PIN. Angaza is never the KRA integrator: every tenant self-onboards on eTIMS under their own PIN and files their own invoices. Not a secret — it appears on every fiscal receipt the business issues.

bhfId.description: Branch id, e.g. "00" for a single-branch business.

dvcSrlNo.description: Device serial number registered with KRA.

initialized.description: Whether KRA has issued this device a communication key. No invoice can be signed until it has.

lastInvoiceNo.description: The last invoice number issued by this device. Numbers are sequential per device and are allocated under a row lock, so two concurrent signs can never take the same one.

invoiceType.description: SALE, or CREDIT_NOTE for the fiscal reversal of a signed sale that was voided.

originalInvoiceId.description: For a CREDIT_NOTE: the SIGNED invoice it reverses. KRA requires a credit note to reference the original and to come from the same solution that filed it.

etimsInvoiceNumber.description: The device's sequential number for this invoice. ALLOCATED BEFORE SUBMISSION AND REUSED ON EVERY RETRY — reallocating one would file the same sale with KRA twice.

status.description: PENDING (number allocated, not yet submitted); SIGNED (KRA signed it — terminal and immutable); REJECTED (KRA was reachable and refused the payload — never auto-retried, an operator fixes and resubmits); QUEUED (KRA was unreachable — retried later with the SAME number); FAILED (retries exhausted).

rcptSign.description: KRA's receipt signature. Present only on SIGNED, and never generated locally.

resultCode.description: KRA's own result code on a rejection. An opaque identifier, not a quantity.

resultMsg.description: Why KRA refused, or why the submission could not be delivered.

alreadySigned.description: true when the sale already had a SIGNED invoice and this call did nothing. A sale is filed with KRA once.

providerName.description: Which implementation signed it: "simulated" in development, "oscu" against real KRA.

keyStored.description: true when the communication key KRA returned was stored into the tenant's encrypted credential blob. The key itself is never returned.

note.description: Why the invoice is not signed, when it is not — eTIMS not configured, KRA unreachable, or KRA's rejection message. Informational only: the sale itself succeeded regardless.

taxRegime.description: VAT_REGISTERED (charges and recovers VAT; purchase receipts capitalise the NET cost and recover input VAT), TURNOVER_TAX (3% turnover-tax regime) or EXEMPT. For the latter two the VAT paid on a purchase is unrecoverable and is therefore part of what the goods cost, so receipts capitalise the VAT-INCLUSIVE figure.

isVatRegistered.description: DERIVED from taxRegime and guaranteed by a database CHECK never to contradict it. Read-only: set taxRegime instead.

kraPin.description: The business's own KRA PIN as printed on its invoices. Public business identity — distinct from the eTIMS integration credential, which is a secret in the encrypted store.

legalName.description: Registered legal name, printed on receipts (Task T-A13).

receiptFooter.description: Printed at the foot of every receipt.

poNumber.description: Sequential per tenant. Monotonic and unique, but NOT gap-free: a rolled-back order burns its number, which is a far smaller problem than two orders sharing one.

status.description: DRAFT (freely editable, no financial effect at all) -> APPROVED (committed to the supplier; may now be received against) -> PARTIALLY_RECEIVED -> RECEIVED -> CLOSED. CANCELLED is reachable only from DRAFT or APPROVED: once goods have arrived the order DID happen and value has been accrued to GRNI, so such an order is CLOSED short instead.

currency.description: Always "KES" today. The column is the multi-currency plug; a CHECK pins it until the FX work is done.

subtotal.description: Sum of the lines' net amounts, in cents.

orderedQty.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

unitCost.description: Cost per unit in KES cents. NET (VAT-exclusive) for a VAT-registered tenant; VAT-INCLUSIVE for a non-registered one, because an unrecoverable tax is part of what the goods cost. In BOTH cases this is exactly the amount that reaches account 1200 on receipt.

lineNet.description: orderedQty x unitCost, rounded once through the single rounding primitive.

receivedQty.description: How much has actually arrived. Moved only by a goods receipt, and capped at orderedQty by a database CHECK.

billedQty.description: How much live (posted, not cancelled) supplier bills have invoiced. billedQty <= receivedQty, held by a CHECK.

unbilledQty.description: receivedQty - billedQty: received but not yet billed — where a new supplier bill against this line starts.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

totalCost.description: The cost this line accrued: the single figure that moved Product.stockValue, was debited to 1200 Inventory and was credited to 2050 GRNI. One valuation event per movement.

totalAccrued.description: Total credited to 2050 GRNI by this receipt — what is now owed to the supplier but not yet invoiced.

GoodsReceiptInput.description: An IMMUTABLE posted fact: goods arrived, stock rose, and value was accrued to GRNI. The database refuses both UPDATE and DELETE on it. A mis-receipt is corrected with a supplier credit (Task 5.2), never by editing history.

billNumber.description: THE SUPPLIER'S OWN invoice reference, not a number we allocate. Unique per supplier, which is the DUPLICATE-PAYMENT GUARD: the same invoice arriving twice cannot become two payables.

dueDate.description: When it falls due, and what the aging report buckets on. Derived from the supplier's payment terms when none is given ("Net 30"), and otherwise equal to billDate — due on receipt, which ages immediately rather than hiding in "current".

status.description: DRAFT (keyed in, NOTHING posted to the ledger, freely editable) -> AWAITING_PAYMENT (posted) -> PARTIALLY_PAID -> PAID. CANCELLED is reachable only while nothing has been paid; cancelling a POSTED bill reverses its journal entry and gives the billed quantity back. PAID and CANCELLED are terminal.

subtotalNet.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

vatTotal.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

total.description: The gross amount owed: subtotalNet + vatTotal, CHECK-enforced. This is the figure credited to 2000 Accounts Payable.

amountPaid.description: Allocated by supplier payments. CHECK-capped at total, so over-paying one invoice is unrepresentable, and a DEFERRED database constraint pins it to the sum of its allocations.

balance.description: total - amountPaid: what is still owed.

currency.description: Always "KES" today; the column is the multi-currency plug and a CHECK pins it.

kind.description: PO_MATCH: goods ordered and received — the line CLEARS 2050 GRNI and does NOT touch inventory, because the goods were already valued when they arrived. EXPENSE: a cost with nothing received against it, debited straight to its own account.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

vatRate.description: The VAT percentage charged on this line, as a decimal STRING. A RATE, NOT MONEY. Always "0.00" for a non-VAT-registered tenant: there is no recoverable tax, and the VAT the supplier charged is already inside lineNet.

lineNet.description: quantity x unit cost, rounded once through the single rounding primitive. VAT-EXCLUSIVE for a VAT-registered tenant; the WHOLE invoiced amount for a non-registered one, because an unrecoverable tax is part of what the purchase cost — the same regime-dependent meaning PurchaseOrderLine.unitCost carries.

lineVat.description: Recoverable input VAT on this line. Always 0 for a non-registered tenant.

unitCostNet.description: The net unit cost the supplier INVOICED, which need not be the unitCost the order agreed and GRNI was accrued at. PO_MATCH lines only.

grniCleared.description: What this line took out of 2050 GRNI. NULL until the bill is posted, and NULL forever on an EXPENSE line. A line that fully bills its purchase order line clears the ENTIRE remaining accrual, so GRNI reaches exactly zero rather than nearly zero.

priceVariance.description: lineNet - grniCleared. Positive means the supplier invoiced MORE than the order agreed. It is posted to 5250 Purchase Price Variance rather than added to stock, because the goods may already have been sold — restating their cost would rewrite a reported margin.

vatRate.description: The VAT percentage charged on this line, as a decimal STRING. A RATE, NOT MONEY. Always "0.00" for a non-VAT-registered tenant: there is no recoverable tax, and the VAT the supplier charged is already inside lineNet.

lineNet.description: quantity x unit cost, rounded once through the single rounding primitive. VAT-EXCLUSIVE for a VAT-registered tenant; the WHOLE invoiced amount for a non-registered one, because an unrecoverable tax is part of what the purchase cost — the same regime-dependent meaning PurchaseOrderLine.unitCost carries.

lineVat.description: Recoverable input VAT on this line. Always 0 for a non-registered tenant.

unitCostNet.description: The net unit cost the supplier INVOICED, which need not be the unitCost the order agreed and GRNI was accrued at. PO_MATCH lines only.

grniCleared.description: What this line took out of 2050 GRNI. NULL until the bill is posted, and NULL forever on an EXPENSE line. A line that fully bills its purchase order line clears the ENTIRE remaining accrual, so GRNI reaches exactly zero rather than nearly zero.

priceVariance.description: lineNet - grniCleared. Positive means the supplier invoiced MORE than the order agreed. It is posted to 5250 Purchase Price Variance rather than added to stock, because the goods may already have been sold — restating their cost would rewrite a reported margin.

journalEntryId.description: The entry that posted this bill, once posted. Derived from the entry's own sourceId rather than stored, so there is no second copy of the link to fall out of step.

paymentNumber.description: Sequential per tenant. Monotonic and unique, NOT gap-free: a rolled-back payment burns its number, which has no regulatory meaning, while two payments sharing one would be a reconciliation defect.

method.description: What selects the credit account: CASH -> 1000 Cash on Hand, BANK -> 1020 Bank Account, MPESA -> 1010 M-Pesa Till. **MPESA RECORDS, IT DOES NOT DISBURSE** — there is no B2B payout here; this is the record of money that went out through M-Pesa.

creditTotal.description: The receivable this sale raised: the SUM of its CREDIT tenders. **DERIVED, never stored** — sale tenders are write-once, so the derivation cannot go stale, and there is no second column that could disagree with them.

arReceived.description: How much has been collected against it. The one mutable AR fact on a sale; a deferred database constraint pins it to the sum of the receipt allocations behind it and caps it at `creditTotal`.

outstanding.description: creditTotal - arReceived: what is still owed.

VOIDED sales are excluded: the void reversed both the receivable and the balance, so showing the charge without the reversal would break the tie-up, and a statement that does not reconcile is worth nothing.

effectiveTo.description: NULL means OPEN-ENDED — the currently in-force ruleset. The window is half-open: [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo).

source.description: Where the figures came from. **Not decoration** — the engineering ledger requires the in-force statutory figures to be verified against an authoritative source at implementation time and the citation recorded, so the next person does not take them on trust. A database CHECK makes a blank citation impossible.

verifiedOn.description: The date the figures were last checked against the source.

personalRelief.description: Monthly personal relief. A RELIEF AGAINST THE TAX, subtracted from the PAYE the bands produce — not a deduction from taxable pay. The engine keeps that distinction because conflating the two changes the answer.

nssfRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

nssfLowerLimit.description: The Tier I / Tier II BOUNDARY, not a floor on the contribution.

shifRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

shifMinimum.description: The statutory MINIMUM monthly contribution. A low earner pays this rather than the percentage.

ahlRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

vatStandardRate.description: The national STANDARD VAT rate for this window (Task 3B.1) — the only copy of that figure in the system. Zero-rated and exempt supplies are tax CLASSES, not rates.

vatRateSource.description: Where the VAT rate came from (statute and authority).

vatRateVerifiedOn.description: When the VAT rate was last verified against that source.

totRatePercent.description: The Turnover Tax rate on gross turnover (Task 3B.2), accrued per sale by a TURNOVER_TAX tenant only. A RATE, never money.

totRateSource.description: Where the TOT rate came from, including any recorded discrepancy between sources.

createdById.description: Who created this version through the API (Task 3B.3). NULL = the system seed (provisioning / migration).

lowerBound.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

upperBound.description: NULL means the top band — unbounded above.

ratePercent.description: A RATE as a decimal string, never money.

bands.description: A CONTIGUOUS, ASCENDING partition of taxable pay from zero, with exactly one open-topped band at the end — enforced by a DEFERRED database constraint, because a gap would tax nothing in it and an overlap would tax the same shillings twice.

StatutoryScheduleInput.description: The effective-dated statutory ruleset — **the single source of every payroll rate in the system**. No statutory figure is a constant in code. EXACTLY ONE schedule may cover any date (a GiST exclusion constraint guarantees it), a payroll run records WHICH schedule computed it, and a rate change is a NEW dated row rather than an edit — so a run for a past period stays correct against the rates in force then. **These routes are READ-ONLY**: a statutory figure is the law of Kenya rather than tenant configuration, so it arrives by the same platform-run seed mechanism as the chart of accounts, never through an API.

employmentType.description: **Monthly salaried is the only shape this task computes.** The enum is the PLUG, so hourly, casual day-rate and contract-specific treatment arrive as new rows and a new engine branch rather than as an ALTER across live employee records.

status.description: ACTIVE employees are included in a NEW payroll run; SUSPENDED and TERMINATED are excluded. Neither deletes anything and neither touches a payslip already computed — those describe months the employee genuinely worked.

basicSalary.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

paymentMethod.description: SNAPSHOTTED onto the employee's net-pay settlement line (Task 8.2) for the bank payment file. It does not select the GL credit account — a run is paid from the ONE account its settlement names.

amount.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

taxable.description: A taxable allowance is part of the pay PAYE is computed on. BOTH kinds are part of gross — and therefore of NSSF, SHIF and the housing levy, which are computed on gross — which is why a payslip carries grossPay and taxableGross as two separate figures.

grossPay.description: basic + EVERY allowance. The base for NSSF, SHIF and the housing levy.

nssfEmployee.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

nssfEmployer.description: MATCHED to the employee's, not computed a second time, so the two can never disagree by a rounding.

nssfTier1.description: The reportable tier split. Computed as a residual so tier1 + tier2 equals the employee contribution EXACTLY (a database CHECK pins it).

nssfTier2.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

ahlEmployer.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

taxablePay.description: taxableGross − NSSF − SHIF − housing levy. **The three statutory employee contributions are ALLOWABLE DEDUCTIONS against taxable pay** under the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2024 — they reduce the income PAYE is computed on, they are NOT reliefs against the tax. A deduction saves tax at the marginal rate; a relief saves it shilling for shilling, so putting them in the wrong place mis-states PAYE for every employee.

payeBeforeRelief.description: PAYE from the bands, each band's own portion rounded once.

personalReliefApplied.description: Capped at payeBeforeRelief: a relief reduces tax to zero, it never becomes a refund.

paye.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

earnings.description: The earnings as they stood WHEN THE RUN WAS COMPUTED — copied, not referenced. A payslip that read through to the live employee record would silently restate itself after a salary revision, so last year's payslip would stop agreeing with last year's journal entry and with what the employee was actually paid.

PayslipInput.description: One employee's computation for one run. EVERY intermediate figure is stored, not just the net: a payslip has to be defensible to the employee and to KRA years later, and recomputing it then would need the engine, the employee's terms AND the schedule exactly as they were. Frozen by a database trigger the moment its run leaves DRAFT.

status.description: DRAFT (computed, NOTHING posted, freely recomputable) -> APPROVED -> POSTED -> PAID. CANCELLED is reachable only before posting. **The accrual is booked ONLY on the APPROVED -> POSTED transition**, which is why a DRAFT can be recomputed as often as the payroll officer likes. **PAID means the NET PAY has been settled** out of 2120 by the run's one net-pay settlement (Task 8.2) — it says nothing about the four statutory heads, which are remitted on their own calendar and read from the run's remittances. PAID and CANCELLED are terminal.

payDate.description: **The accrual entry is dated to it**, because that is the date the obligation is settled against.

statutoryScheduleLabel.description: WHICH ruleset computed this run. Immutable once set: a payslip can only be re-derived if the rates it used are knowable.

journalEntryId.description: The accrual entry, set on posting and never again.

grossPay.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

employerContributions.description: Employer NSSF + employer housing levy — the cost ON TOP of gross.

leaseExpiresAt.description: leaseStartedAt + the location's window AT THE TIME CUSTODY WAS TAKEN. NULL means FOREVER and never expires. Editing the location's policy later does not move a live lease.

holdsCustody.description: true while a lease has been started and not ended. A device holding no custody cannot block a period close.

leaseExpired.description: true only when a NON-NULL expiry is in the past. A forever lease is never expired. An expired lease whose stock has been frozen reads false here, because the freeze ends the lease — the freeze row is where that state lives.

status.description: PENDING_RECONCILIATION (live — immobilised, awaiting the truth or a decision), RELEASED_BY_SYNC (the device synced; real sales posted and the remainder went back to MAIN), or WRITTEN_OFF (an admin posted the loss, Dr 5300 / Cr 1200).

leaseExpiredAt.description: The lease expiry that triggered this freeze.

productCount.description: How many product slices were immobilised when the freeze was taken.

resolvedBy.description: NULL on a sync release — nobody decided anything, the device simply reported what it sold. Always set on a write-off: an accounting loss names its decider.

outcome.description: POSTED (became a real Sale through the atomic sale transaction), REPLAYED (this key had already posted — a no-op, no second journal entry and no second stock decrement), or NEEDS_RESOLUTION (could not post; NOTHING was posted and the capture is queued for the owner).

businessTimestamp.description: When the sale actually happened — preserved exactly as captured.

entryDate.description: The date the journal entry was DATED to. Null when nothing posted.

postedToCurrentPeriod.description: true when the closed-period fallback was taken: this capture's own period had already closed, so the entry posted into the current open period instead of being dropped.

originalBusinessDate.description: The true business date, recorded on the sale when the fallback was taken.

fiscalStatus.description: The sale's resulting KRA fiscal status, or NOT_ATTEMPTED when eTIMS could not be tried (the tenant has not configured it).

etims.description: Present only for a capture that requested a KRA invoice (Task 4.1). A device cannot sign — eTIMS needs KRA — so the SERVER signs on sync, as a deferred online operation through the same signSaleInvoice the online POS uses. A signing failure NEVER changes the sale's outcome above: the sale is already committed and final.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

freezeResolution.description: Present only when this sync met an active lease freeze over the device's location.

payload.description: The exact captured payload that was attempted, as JSON, so the owner can see what the sale was. Money and quantities inside it are strings, as everywhere.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

totalCost.description: The carrying value written off for this product — the amount posted Dr 5300 / Cr 1200.

totalWrittenOff.description: Total posted to 5300 Inventory Write-offs by this write-off, in cents.

tin.description: The TENANT's own KRA PIN. Angaza is never the KRA integrator: every tenant self-onboards on eTIMS under their own PIN and files their own invoices. Not a secret — it appears on every fiscal receipt the business issues.

bhfId.description: Branch id, e.g. "00" for a single-branch business.

dvcSrlNo.description: Device serial number registered with KRA.

initialized.description: Whether KRA has issued this device a communication key. No invoice can be signed until it has.

lastInvoiceNo.description: The last invoice number issued by this device. Numbers are sequential per device and are allocated under a row lock, so two concurrent signs can never take the same one.

invoiceType.description: SALE, or CREDIT_NOTE for the fiscal reversal of a signed sale that was voided.

originalInvoiceId.description: For a CREDIT_NOTE: the SIGNED invoice it reverses. KRA requires a credit note to reference the original and to come from the same solution that filed it.

etimsInvoiceNumber.description: The device's sequential number for this invoice. ALLOCATED BEFORE SUBMISSION AND REUSED ON EVERY RETRY — reallocating one would file the same sale with KRA twice.

status.description: PENDING (number allocated, not yet submitted); SIGNED (KRA signed it — terminal and immutable); REJECTED (KRA was reachable and refused the payload — never auto-retried, an operator fixes and resubmits); QUEUED (KRA was unreachable — retried later with the SAME number); FAILED (retries exhausted).

rcptSign.description: KRA's receipt signature. Present only on SIGNED, and never generated locally.

resultCode.description: KRA's own result code on a rejection. An opaque identifier, not a quantity.

resultMsg.description: Why KRA refused, or why the submission could not be delivered.

alreadySigned.description: true when the sale already had a SIGNED invoice and this call did nothing. A sale is filed with KRA once.

providerName.description: Which implementation signed it: "simulated" in development, "oscu" against real KRA.

keyStored.description: true when the communication key KRA returned was stored into the tenant's encrypted credential blob. The key itself is never returned.

note.description: Why the invoice is not signed, when it is not — eTIMS not configured, KRA unreachable, or KRA's rejection message. Informational only: the sale itself succeeded regardless.

taxRegime.description: VAT_REGISTERED (charges and recovers VAT; purchase receipts capitalise the NET cost and recover input VAT), TURNOVER_TAX (3% turnover-tax regime) or EXEMPT. For the latter two the VAT paid on a purchase is unrecoverable and is therefore part of what the goods cost, so receipts capitalise the VAT-INCLUSIVE figure.

isVatRegistered.description: DERIVED from taxRegime and guaranteed by a database CHECK never to contradict it. Read-only: set taxRegime instead.

kraPin.description: The business's own KRA PIN as printed on its invoices. Public business identity — distinct from the eTIMS integration credential, which is a secret in the encrypted store.

legalName.description: Registered legal name, printed on receipts (Task T-A13).

receiptFooter.description: Printed at the foot of every receipt.

poNumber.description: Sequential per tenant. Monotonic and unique, but NOT gap-free: a rolled-back order burns its number, which is a far smaller problem than two orders sharing one.

status.description: DRAFT (freely editable, no financial effect at all) -> APPROVED (committed to the supplier; may now be received against) -> PARTIALLY_RECEIVED -> RECEIVED -> CLOSED. CANCELLED is reachable only from DRAFT or APPROVED: once goods have arrived the order DID happen and value has been accrued to GRNI, so such an order is CLOSED short instead.

currency.description: Always "KES" today. The column is the multi-currency plug; a CHECK pins it until the FX work is done.

subtotal.description: Sum of the lines' net amounts, in cents.

orderedQty.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

unitCost.description: Cost per unit in KES cents. NET (VAT-exclusive) for a VAT-registered tenant; VAT-INCLUSIVE for a non-registered one, because an unrecoverable tax is part of what the goods cost. In BOTH cases this is exactly the amount that reaches account 1200 on receipt.

lineNet.description: orderedQty x unitCost, rounded once through the single rounding primitive.

receivedQty.description: How much has actually arrived. Moved only by a goods receipt, and capped at orderedQty by a database CHECK.

billedQty.description: How much live (posted, not cancelled) supplier bills have invoiced. billedQty <= receivedQty, held by a CHECK.

unbilledQty.description: receivedQty - billedQty: received but not yet billed — where a new supplier bill against this line starts.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

totalCost.description: The cost this line accrued: the single figure that moved Product.stockValue, was debited to 1200 Inventory and was credited to 2050 GRNI. One valuation event per movement.

totalAccrued.description: Total credited to 2050 GRNI by this receipt — what is now owed to the supplier but not yet invoiced.

GoodsReceipt.description: An IMMUTABLE posted fact: goods arrived, stock rose, and value was accrued to GRNI. The database refuses both UPDATE and DELETE on it. A mis-receipt is corrected with a supplier credit (Task 5.2), never by editing history.

billNumber.description: THE SUPPLIER'S OWN invoice reference, not a number we allocate. Unique per supplier, which is the DUPLICATE-PAYMENT GUARD: the same invoice arriving twice cannot become two payables.

dueDate.description: When it falls due, and what the aging report buckets on. Derived from the supplier's payment terms when none is given ("Net 30"), and otherwise equal to billDate — due on receipt, which ages immediately rather than hiding in "current".

status.description: DRAFT (keyed in, NOTHING posted to the ledger, freely editable) -> AWAITING_PAYMENT (posted) -> PARTIALLY_PAID -> PAID. CANCELLED is reachable only while nothing has been paid; cancelling a POSTED bill reverses its journal entry and gives the billed quantity back. PAID and CANCELLED are terminal.

subtotalNet.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

vatTotal.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

total.description: The gross amount owed: subtotalNet + vatTotal, CHECK-enforced. This is the figure credited to 2000 Accounts Payable.

amountPaid.description: Allocated by supplier payments. CHECK-capped at total, so over-paying one invoice is unrepresentable, and a DEFERRED database constraint pins it to the sum of its allocations.

balance.description: total - amountPaid: what is still owed.

currency.description: Always "KES" today; the column is the multi-currency plug and a CHECK pins it.

kind.description: PO_MATCH: goods ordered and received — the line CLEARS 2050 GRNI and does NOT touch inventory, because the goods were already valued when they arrived. EXPENSE: a cost with nothing received against it, debited straight to its own account.

quantity.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

vatRate.description: The VAT percentage charged on this line, as a decimal STRING. A RATE, NOT MONEY. Always "0.00" for a non-VAT-registered tenant: there is no recoverable tax, and the VAT the supplier charged is already inside lineNet.

lineVat.description: Recoverable input VAT on this line. Always 0 for a non-registered tenant.

unitCostNet.description: The net unit cost the supplier INVOICED, which need not be the unitCost the order agreed and GRNI was accrued at. PO_MATCH lines only.

grniCleared.description: What this line took out of 2050 GRNI. NULL until the bill is posted, and NULL forever on an EXPENSE line. A line that fully bills its purchase order line clears the ENTIRE remaining accrual, so GRNI reaches exactly zero rather than nearly zero.

priceVariance.description: lineNet - grniCleared. Positive means the supplier invoiced MORE than the order agreed. It is posted to 5250 Purchase Price Variance rather than added to stock, because the goods may already have been sold — restating their cost would rewrite a reported margin.

paymentNumber.description: Sequential per tenant. Monotonic and unique, NOT gap-free: a rolled-back payment burns its number, which has no regulatory meaning, while two payments sharing one would be a reconciliation defect.

grandTotal.description: The sum of every unpaid bill balance. **This is the AP that supplier bills have put into account 2000**, and the two reconciling is the acceptance criterion for the whole module.

ApAging.description: Bucketed by DUE date over unpaid balances, per supplier. Only AWAITING_PAYMENT and PARTIALLY_PAID bills appear: a DRAFT posted nothing, a CANCELLED bill has been reversed, a PAID one is settled — including any of them would make the report disagree with account 2000.

charged.description: What the invoice added to what is owed. 0 on a payment.

paid.description: What the payment took off. 0 on a bill.

runningBalance.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

totalPaid.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

closingBalance.description: totalCharged - totalPaid, which equals this supplier's unpaid bill balances and therefore their slice of the aging report and of account 2000.

SupplierStatement.description: Every POSTED invoice and every payment in date order with a running balance. DRAFT and CANCELLED bills are excluded: a cancelled bill's entry has been reversed, so showing its charge without the reversal would make the closing balance disagree with account 2000 — and a statement that does not reconcile is worth nothing.

saleDate.description: The business date the receivable arose: the sale's `businessTimestamp` when it came from an offline device (that is when the customer actually took the goods), otherwise `createdAt`. Ageing an offline sale from its sync time would make a three-day-old debt look fresh.

saleTotal.description: The sale's full value, for context. **NOT the receivable** — a sale can be part cash, part credit.

creditTotal.description: The receivable this sale raised: the SUM of its CREDIT tenders. **DERIVED, never stored** — sale tenders are write-once, so the derivation cannot go stale, and there is no second column that could disagree with them.

arReceived.description: How much has been collected against it. The one mutable AR fact on a sale; a deferred database constraint pins it to the sum of the receipt allocations behind it and caps it at `creditTotal`.

outstanding.description: creditTotal - arReceived: what is still owed.

receiptNumber.description: Sequential per tenant. Monotonic and unique, NOT gap-free: a rolled-back receipt burns its number, which has no regulatory meaning, while two receipts sharing one would be a reconciliation defect.

method.description: What selects the debit account: CASH -> 1000 Cash on Hand, BANK -> 1020 Bank Account, MPESA -> 1010 M-Pesa Till. **MPESA RECORDS, IT DOES NOT COLLECT** — there is no STK Pull here. The POS sale path's live STK Push (Task 3.3) is a different operation: that collects at the till for a sale being rung up, this records a customer paying down an account they already owe.

grandTotal.description: The sum of every open credit sale's outstanding amount. **It equals SUM(Customer.creditBalance)**, and both equal GL(1100) MINUS the M-Pesa-failure residual — the AR that a failed STK Push posted to 1100 with no customer attribution (Task 3.3). See the engineering ledger "Accounts Receivable".

ArAging.description: Bucketed by SALE date over per-sale outstanding amounts, grouped by customer. Aged by sale date rather than a due date because `Customer` carries no payment terms — inventing one would bake a guess into live data. Only COMPLETED credit sales appear: a VOIDED sale's receivable was reversed.

charged.description: What the credit sale added to what is owed — the CREDIT portion only, never the sale total. 0 on a receipt.

received.description: What the receipt took off. 0 on a sale.

runningBalance.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

creditBalance.description: The live column, so a reader can see the statement tie to it.

creditLimit.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

CustomerStatement.description: Every credit sale and every receipt in date order with a running balance. Only the CREDIT PORTION of each sale appears — a sale paid half in cash put only the credit half on the account. VOIDED sales are excluded: the void reversed both the receivable and the balance, so showing the charge without the reversal would break the tie-up, and a statement that does not reconcile is worth nothing.

effectiveTo.description: NULL means OPEN-ENDED — the currently in-force ruleset. The window is half-open: [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo).

source.description: Where the figures came from. **Not decoration** — the engineering ledger requires the in-force statutory figures to be verified against an authoritative source at implementation time and the citation recorded, so the next person does not take them on trust. A database CHECK makes a blank citation impossible.

verifiedOn.description: The date the figures were last checked against the source.

personalRelief.description: Monthly personal relief. A RELIEF AGAINST THE TAX, subtracted from the PAYE the bands produce — not a deduction from taxable pay. The engine keeps that distinction because conflating the two changes the answer.

nssfRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

nssfLowerLimit.description: The Tier I / Tier II BOUNDARY, not a floor on the contribution.

shifRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

shifMinimum.description: The statutory MINIMUM monthly contribution. A low earner pays this rather than the percentage.

ahlRatePercent.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

vatStandardRate.description: The national STANDARD VAT rate for this window (Task 3B.1) — the only copy of that figure in the system. Zero-rated and exempt supplies are tax CLASSES, not rates.

vatRateSource.description: Where the VAT rate came from (statute and authority).

vatRateVerifiedOn.description: When the VAT rate was last verified against that source.

totRatePercent.description: The Turnover Tax rate on gross turnover (Task 3B.2), accrued per sale by a TURNOVER_TAX tenant only. A RATE, never money.

totRateSource.description: Where the TOT rate came from, including any recorded discrepancy between sources.

createdById.description: Who created this version through the API (Task 3B.3). NULL = the system seed (provisioning / migration).

lowerBound.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

upperBound.description: NULL means the top band — unbounded above.

ratePercent.description: A RATE as a decimal string, never money.

bands.description: A CONTIGUOUS, ASCENDING partition of taxable pay from zero, with exactly one open-topped band at the end — enforced by a DEFERRED database constraint, because a gap would tax nothing in it and an overlap would tax the same shillings twice.

StatutorySchedule.description: The effective-dated statutory ruleset — **the single source of every payroll rate in the system**. No statutory figure is a constant in code. EXACTLY ONE schedule may cover any date (a GiST exclusion constraint guarantees it), a payroll run records WHICH schedule computed it, and a rate change is a NEW dated row rather than an edit — so a run for a past period stays correct against the rates in force then. **These routes are READ-ONLY**: a statutory figure is the law of Kenya rather than tenant configuration, so it arrives by the same platform-run seed mechanism as the chart of accounts, never through an API.

employmentType.description: **Monthly salaried is the only shape this task computes.** The enum is the PLUG, so hourly, casual day-rate and contract-specific treatment arrive as new rows and a new engine branch rather than as an ALTER across live employee records.

status.description: ACTIVE employees are included in a NEW payroll run; SUSPENDED and TERMINATED are excluded. Neither deletes anything and neither touches a payslip already computed — those describe months the employee genuinely worked.

paymentMethod.description: SNAPSHOTTED onto the employee's net-pay settlement line (Task 8.2) for the bank payment file. It does not select the GL credit account — a run is paid from the ONE account its settlement names.

amount.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

taxable.description: A taxable allowance is part of the pay PAYE is computed on. BOTH kinds are part of gross — and therefore of NSSF, SHIF and the housing levy, which are computed on gross — which is why a payslip carries grossPay and taxableGross as two separate figures.

grossPay.description: basic + EVERY allowance. The base for NSSF, SHIF and the housing levy.

nssfEmployer.description: MATCHED to the employee's, not computed a second time, so the two can never disagree by a rounding.

nssfTier1.description: The reportable tier split. Computed as a residual so tier1 + tier2 equals the employee contribution EXACTLY (a database CHECK pins it).

taxablePay.description: taxableGross − NSSF − SHIF − housing levy. **The three statutory employee contributions are ALLOWABLE DEDUCTIONS against taxable pay** under the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2024 — they reduce the income PAYE is computed on, they are NOT reliefs against the tax. A deduction saves tax at the marginal rate; a relief saves it shilling for shilling, so putting them in the wrong place mis-states PAYE for every employee.

payeBeforeRelief.description: PAYE from the bands, each band's own portion rounded once.

personalReliefApplied.description: Capped at payeBeforeRelief: a relief reduces tax to zero, it never becomes a refund.

earnings.description: The earnings as they stood WHEN THE RUN WAS COMPUTED — copied, not referenced. A payslip that read through to the live employee record would silently restate itself after a salary revision, so last year's payslip would stop agreeing with last year's journal entry and with what the employee was actually paid.

Payslip.description: One employee's computation for one run. EVERY intermediate figure is stored, not just the net: a payslip has to be defensible to the employee and to KRA years later, and recomputing it then would need the engine, the employee's terms AND the schedule exactly as they were. Frozen by a database trigger the moment its run leaves DRAFT.

status.description: DRAFT (computed, NOTHING posted, freely recomputable) -> APPROVED -> POSTED -> PAID. CANCELLED is reachable only before posting. **The accrual is booked ONLY on the APPROVED -> POSTED transition**, which is why a DRAFT can be recomputed as often as the payroll officer likes. **PAID means the NET PAY has been settled** out of 2120 by the run's one net-pay settlement (Task 8.2) — it says nothing about the four statutory heads, which are remitted on their own calendar and read from the run's remittances. PAID and CANCELLED are terminal.

method.description: SNAPSHOT of how this employee is paid, taken at settlement. Recorded for the bank payment file a later task builds; the ledger is NOT split by it.

lines.description: ONE audit line per payslip of the run — every employee is accounted for, including one whose net is zero.

NetPayPayment.description: The settlement of ONE run's net pay — exactly one per run, IMMUTABLE once written. It posts `Dr 2120 Net Salaries Payable / Cr 1000|1020|1010` and moves the run POSTED -> PAID in the same transaction. It touches no stock table, no 1200, no revenue and no expense account: the cost was recognised by the accrual.

post.summary: Log in — a token pair, or the next login step
post.description: Public. Rate-limited per IP+email. When the account owes nothing more, a session (status AUTHENTICATED): the accessToken carries the user, role and tenant, and every other endpoint derives the tenant schema from it, never from a request field. Otherwise (M4.5 W1) a challenge naming the next step: MFA_REQUIRED, PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED (forced reset on first login) or MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED (a SUPER_ADMIN or PROGRAM_OFFICER without MFA — they can never sign in without a second factor).

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 expiry of the refresh token.

schema.description: Either a session (status AUTHENTICATED) or a challenge naming the next step.

post.summary: Login stage: prove the second factor
post.description: Public, rate-limited per IP. A 6-digit authenticator code (each code is accepted ONCE — a replay is refused) or an unused backup code (burned on use). A wrong code counts against the challenge; after LOGIN_CHALLENGE_MAX_ATTEMPTS it is burned and the user signs in again with their password.

post.summary: Close an accounting period
post.description:
A closed period rejects further postings at the database level.

**409 — business-time integrity guard (Task OFF.1).** The close is REFUSED while any ACTIVE offline device still holds a LIVE lease that could carry sales dated inside the period and has not synced past its end. Closing then would assert a complete month over sales the server knows may exist. Have each device sync, or end its lease (`POST /v1/offline/devices/:id/lease/end`), then close.

An EXPIRED lease does NOT block: expiry freezes the device's stock to PENDING_RECONCILIATION and raises it for a decision, so what it may be carrying is known and flagged rather than unknown — and anything that arrives later posts into the current open period with its true business date recorded on the sale.

A deactivated location cannot be a transfer source, so stock left on one would be stranded — owned by a location that can no longer send it anywhere, yet still counted in Product.stockCount and carried in GL account 1200. The MAIN pool can never be deactivated. Deactivating an already-inactive location is a no-op.
The symmetric counterpart to /deactivate. Needs no guard: an inactive location owns no stock (that is what deactivation required). Reactivating an already-active location is a no-op.

post.summary: Allocate stock to a location (direct, no prior request)
post.description:
An admin pushing stock into a selling location. This IS a transfer — the value-neutral TRANSFER_OUT/TRANSFER_IN pair from Task 10.1 — wrapped in allocation semantics:

* **No journal entry.** Nothing was bought or sold; the goods are simply held somewhere else.
* **Product.stockCount, stockValue and avgCost are unchanged.** Only the per-location split moves, so `sum(stockValue) = GL(1200)` keeps holding.
* **Two immutable stock movements** are written, so the allocation is fully auditable.

Rejected with 400 if the source location does not own enough, naming the available quantity — nothing sells or sends stock it does not own.

fromLocationId.description: Defaults to the tenant's MAIN pool. Name another location to move stock between two selling locations.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.
Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

fromQuantityAfter.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

toQuantityAfter.description: Decimal value as a string (quantity or percentage rate; never money).

sourceDefaulted.description: true when no fromLocationId was given and the MAIN pool was used.

productStockCount.description: The tenant-wide aggregate. An allocation NEVER changes it — only the per-location split moves.

post.summary: Request more stock into a location
post.description:
An attendant asking for a top-up. **This moves NO stock.** Nothing is transferred, nothing is reserved, no stock movement is written and no journal entry is posted — the request is a proposal that lands in the admin's queue as PENDING. Stock moves only when an admin approves it.

The MAIN pool cannot be the requesting location: a request asks for stock to be moved INTO a selling location, out of the pool.

**A CASHIER may request only for their own assigned location** (M4.5 W3): any other `locationId`, or no assignment, is 403.

requestedQty.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

get.summary: List allocation requests
get.description: Newest first. Filter by status (`PENDING` is the admin's queue), by location, or by product.

get.summary: Get one allocation request

post.summary: Approve or decline a pending allocation request
post.description:
**APPROVED** transfers the granted quantity from MAIN into the requesting location and links the resulting TRANSFER_IN movement as `transferId`. The status flip and the transfer happen in ONE transaction: a request can never read APPROVED without its stock having moved, and stock can never move against a request still in the queue. The transfer is value-neutral — no journal entry, aggregate and carrying value untouched.

**DECLINED** records the decision and moves nothing.

Omit `approvedQty` to grant the full request; supply it to edit the grant.

**409** if the request is not PENDING — a decided request is final, and a second decide is refused (the database enforces this too, so two concurrent approvals cannot both transfer).

**400** if MAIN does not own enough for the approved quantity: the transaction rolls back, nothing moves, and the request STAYS PENDING so it can be approved for less or after a restock. A failed approval is not a decision.

approvedQty.description: Approvals only. Omit to grant the full requested quantity; supply a different figure to edit the grant down (or up).

post.summary: Cancel your own pending allocation request
post.description: The requester withdraws a request before it is decided. Moves no stock. **403** if the caller did not create the request — an admin declines it instead of cancelling it, so the queue records which of the two happened. **409** if it is no longer PENDING.

get.summary: The allocation admin's alert feed
get.description:
Everything needing the admin's attention: per-location slices at or below their reorder threshold, plus the pending-request queue.

**This is DATA, not delivery.** Push, email and SMS notification is a later notifications module; this endpoint is what that module — and the dashboard — will read.

The threshold is `Product.minStockThreshold`, the catalog's existing reorder point, applied PER LOCATION SLICE. A threshold of **zero raises no alert**: without that rule every product would alarm at every location it has never stocked, and a feed that is always full is a feed nobody reads. A location reaching zero is separately a hard stop at the point of sale — that is the selling guard, not an alert.

post.summary: Close a till shift and compute the cash variance
post.description: expectedCash = openingFloat + cash taken - cash refunded; variance = closingFloat - expectedCash (signed).

post.summary: Record a sale
post.description:
Decrements stock, posts COGS and revenue through the ledger, and records tenders — all in one transaction. An MPESA tender is created PENDING and settles to 1015 M-Pesa Clearing until its STK callback confirms it. quantity, discount and amount are decimal strings.

**The sale draws from a selling location.** `sellingLocationId` defaults to the tenant's MAIN pool, so a request that omits it behaves exactly as before. Stock comes out of that location's OWNED quantity and is checked against it — **a till holding 5 cannot sell 6 even when the warehouse holds 500**, because a location sells only what it owns. That refusal is a 400 naming the location, the requested quantity and the owned quantity.

Valuation is unaffected: COGS still derives from the product's tenant-wide authoritative stockValue, and a location running dry while the tenant still holds stock is an ordinary partial movement, not a depletion.

sellingLocationId.description: Which location is selling. Omit for the tenant's MAIN pool — the behaviour before this field existed. The sale draws from THIS location's OWNED stock, so it is refused with 400 if this location lacks the quantity even when the tenant holds plenty elsewhere. Recorded on the sale so a void returns the goods here.

requestEtims.description:
**THE PER-SALE KRA eTIMS OPT-IN (Task 4.1).** Set it when the customer wants a KRA fiscal invoice — usually because they will claim the expense, which is why a buyer PIN normally accompanies it.

**Omit it for the ordinary sale.** Most MSME sales are informal, carry no buyer PIN and are validly finalized with no fiscal invoice: `fiscalStatus` stays NOT_REQUESTED and nothing is sent to KRA. The system never auto-submits every sale.

When set, the sale is recorded and committed FIRST and the invoice is signed AFTERWARDS, outside the sale transaction. **A signing failure never fails the sale** — the response still reports 201 with the sale, plus an `etims` note saying what happened. eTIMS posts nothing to the ledger: the VAT was already posted at sale time.

get.summary: Every active cashier of this business and the location they sell from

put.summary: Assign (or reassign) a cashier to a selling location
put.description: Takes effect at once. A cashier sells only from this location: their quote, sale and stock request name it or nothing, and their shift opens here. A shift they opened at their OLD location can no longer ring a sale — they close it and open one here. Any active location except a storefront. Another business's user, a non-cashier or an inactive account is 404.

delete.description: They can open no new shift until assigned again. A shift already open stays open but can ring no further sale.

get.summary: The till I sell from, what is running low there, and my stock requests
get.description: A CASHIER: their assigned location (null if not assigned), its low-stock slices (the same threshold rule as the admin feed — a zero threshold raises nothing) and their own allocation requests, newest first. An owner or manager is not restricted (`restricted: false`, location null); they read the admin feed at GET /v1/allocations/low-stock.

post.summary: Register an offline POS device
post.description:
Binds a device to ONE offline-capable location. That location's owned stock IS the device's allocation, and the device sells nothing else — which is what makes offline conflict-free: no other channel can touch the slice it sells from.

**400** if the location is not offline-capable. MAIN and ECOMMERCE can never be: the pool is server-held and a storefront is server-side, and attaching a lease clock (and therefore a possible freeze) to the tenant's authoritative pool would put the pool itself at risk. A database trigger enforces this too.

Registering moves no stock, reserves nothing and posts nothing.

locationId.description: The OFFLINE-CAPABLE location this device serves. Its owned stock IS the device's allocation. Refused for MAIN and ECOMMERCE, which can never be offline-capable, and for any location whose isOfflineCapable is false.

get.summary: List devices with their lease status
get.description: Every registered device, its location, and its custody state. `leaseExpiresAt` NULL means FOREVER — a lease that never expires (a permanent branch warehouse). `holdsCustody` is what the period-close guard looks at.

get.summary: Get one device

post.summary: Take custody of this location's allocation (start the lease)
post.description:
**This is the fact the lease policy was waiting for.** Task 10.2 stored a per-location `leaseWindowMinutes` and enforced nothing, because nothing yet knew when a lease STARTED. A device taking custody is that moment:

* `leaseStartedAt = now`
* `leaseExpiresAt = now + the location's leaseWindowMinutes`
* a **NULL** window yields a **NULL** expiry — FOREVER, which never expires and never freezes.

The expiry is a SNAPSHOT of the policy at this moment. An admin editing the location's window afterwards changes the next lease, not this one — the alternative would retroactively expire a till that is mid-shift.

Custody moves NO stock and posts nothing: the location already owns the stock (that was the allocation). This records that a device is now answerable for it.

**409** for a SUSPENDED or RETIRED device. It may still sync what it already captured; it may not be handed a fresh window to sell in.

post.summary: Renew the lease (take custody again)
post.description: Identical to starting a lease, and deliberately so: a renewal IS taking custody again. The clock restarts from the moment the device last proved it was there, not from some earlier grant, and it re-reads the location's CURRENT window.

post.summary: Hand in the lease (end custody)
post.description:
The clean counterpart to expiry: the device is back on the network, has handed in what it had, and is no longer answerable for a window. It moves no stock — the location still owns whatever it owns — and posts nothing.

This is also what UNBLOCKS A PERIOD CLOSE: a device holding no custody can no longer be carrying unsynced sales nobody has accounted for. Sync first, then end the lease, then close the period.

post.summary: Ingest a batch of captured offline sales
post.description:
Replays captured sales through the **EXISTING atomic sale transaction** — the same one an online sale uses, under the same database triggers. An offline sale becomes a journal entry only here, on the server, and there is no second posting path.

**The selling location comes from the DEVICE**, never from the request. Each capture draws stock from the device's location and is checked against what that location OWNS (Task 3.2-LOC). Because the device only ever sold stock its location already owned — allocated to it before it went offline, and unsellable by any other channel — **the server-side stock re-validation cannot fail in the normal case**: the stock was reserved before the sale was made. There is no shared pool to race for, so there is no conflict to resolve.

**ORDER:** oldest `businessTimestamp` first, so periods fill in the order things actually happened.

**BUSINESS-TIME POSTING:** each journal entry is DATED to its capture's `businessTimestamp`; `syncedAt` is recorded separately on the sale. The two are never conflated.

**IDEMPOTENCY:** a key that has already posted returns `REPLAYED` — no second journal entry, no second stock decrement, no error — so a device may retry freely on a bad connection. A unique index enforces it, not a convention.

**CLOSED-PERIOD FALLBACK:** a capture whose own period has already closed posts into the CURRENT open period, with the true date recorded on the sale as `originalBusinessDate` and referenced in the entry's description. The record is never lost and the real date stays auditable.

**NEEDS_RESOLUTION:** a capture that cannot post (its shift has closed, its location genuinely cannot cover it, its clock is in the future, both periods are shut) posts NOTHING — no journal entry, no stock movement, nothing negative — and is queued with its exact payload at `GET /v1/offline/needs-resolution`. It is never dropped.

**FREEZE RESOLUTION:** if this device's location was frozen by an expired lease, a sync that accounts for everything releases it — the real sales post and the genuinely unsold remainder returns to MAIN as a value-neutral transfer. If ANY capture lands in the queue, the freeze is KEPT: part of the allocation is already spoken for, and returning it to MAIN while holding evidence it was sold is exactly the guess the server refuses to make.

One transaction per sale — a batch is a transport convenience, not a unit of work.

idempotencyKey.description: The device's own unique key for this sale. Replaying it is a no-op — no second journal entry, no second stock decrement — which is what makes at-least-once delivery safe. Enforced by a unique index, not by convention.

businessTimestamp.description: When the sale ACTUALLY happened at the till. The journal entry is DATED to this, so a sale made two days ago posts two days ago, into that accounting period. A timestamp in the future is queued rather than accepted.

shiftId.description: The shift the sale was rung on. It must still be OPEN: a closed shift carries a counted, signed-off cash variance, and a late cash sale would falsify it. A capture whose shift has closed goes to the resolution queue — never dropped, never posted into a settled reconciliation.

requestEtims.description: The per-sale KRA eTIMS opt-in, captured OFFLINE (Task 4.1). A device cannot sign — eTIMS needs KRA — so it records only that the customer asked, and the SERVER signs on sync, after the sale posts through the atomic transaction. This is the deferred online operation the offline design anticipated: there is no second signing path. If KRA is unreachable when the batch arrives, the invoice QUEUES with its allocated number, which is simply the ordinary connectivity case.

discount.description: Non-negative KES amount as a decimal string with at most 2 decimal places. Stored as integer minor units (cents). Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

amount.description: Non-negative KES amount as a decimal string with at most 2 decimal places. Stored as integer minor units (cents). Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.
