get.summary: Per-device sync and lease state, plus frozen-allocation alerts
get.description:
The transparency surface. Per device: its custody state, whether its location is FROZEN pending reconciliation, how many of its captures are in the owner's queue, and how many have posted.

`activeFreezes` is the admin's alert feed for frozen allocation, with the per-product detail of what each freeze holds. **This is DATA, not delivery** — push/email/SMS is a later notifications module, exactly as with the low-stock feed.

status.description: PENDING_RECONCILIATION (live — immobilised, awaiting the truth or a decision), RELEASED_BY_SYNC (the device synced; real sales posted and the remainder went back to MAIN), or WRITTEN_OFF (an admin posted the loss, Dr 5300 / Cr 1200).

leaseExpiredAt.description: The lease expiry that triggered this freeze.

productCount.description: How many product slices were immobilised when the freeze was taken.

resolvedBy.description: NULL on a sync release — nobody decided anything, the device simply reported what it sold. Always set on a write-off: an accounting loss names its decider.

frozenQuantity.description: The immobilised quantity at this location — removed from its sellable allocation.

ownedQuantity.description: Total still OWNED at this location. A freeze does not change it, which is why Product.stockCount = SUM(per-location quantity) and sum(stockValue) = GL(1200) both survive a freeze untouched.

frozen.description: What is immobilised right now. Empty once the freeze has resolved.

post.summary: Write off a device's frozen allocation (lost, stolen or dead device)
post.description:
The one-click admin resolution for a freeze that will never resolve itself. **This is the ONLY path by which frozen stock becomes a general-ledger event.**

One `WRITE_OFF` movement per frozen product slice, each posting **Dr 5300 Inventory Write-offs / Cr 1200 Inventory** at carrying value — the ordinary outbound path through the inventory service, with no special valuation and no new accounts. `sum(Product.stockValue) = GL(1200)` still holds after the loss is taken, because the credit to 1200 IS the reduction in stockValue (one valuation event per movement).

ONE transaction: the movements, the journal entries and the freeze's resolution commit together. The caller's user id is recorded as `resolvedBy` — an accounting loss always names the person who decided to take it.

**409** if the device's location holds no live freeze (for instance because the device has since synced, which released it automatically).

reason.description: Why the stock is being written off. A write-off is a recorded business decision and always names both its reason and its decider.
reason.example: Tablet stolen from Till 1 on 2026-09-28; police report filed.

get.summary: Captured sales that could not post
get.description:
The owner's queue, oldest business time first. **Nothing in here has had any financial effect** — no journal entry, no stock movement, no sale — so nothing in here can be making a balance wrong. They are sales that HAPPENED and have not yet been recorded, which is a different and visible problem.

Each row carries the exact captured payload that was attempted and the reason it could not post. A capture in this queue is NOT consumed: re-sending the same `idempotencyKey` is allowed to try again, which is how the queue clears itself once the blocking condition (a freeze, a closed shift, a shut period) is gone.

post.summary: Initialize this tenant's OSCU device with KRA
post.description:
Calls KRA's `selectInitOsdcInfo(tin, bhfId, dvcSrlNo)` and stores the **communication key (cmcKey)** it returns back into this tenant's own encrypted credential blob. Every later invoice carries that key.

**STATEFUL AND OCCASIONAL** — run at setup, or when a key expires. It is never part of signing a sale.

**The key is never returned.** The response reports only that it was stored; the secret stays in the credential store, as every secret in this system does.

**Angaza is never the KRA integrator.** The TIN, branch and device serial all come from THIS tenant's credentials, stored under `/v1/integrations/ETIMS` — there is no Angaza-level eTIMS credential and no shared signer. **400** if the tenant has not stored active credentials, or if KRA refuses or cannot be reached.

get.summary: This tenant's eTIMS device and its invoice counter
get.description: The device's non-secret identity, whether it has been initialized, and the last invoice number it issued. **404** when the tenant has never initialized a device — which is the normal state for a business that does not use eTIMS.

post.summary: File a sale with KRA (opt-in, per sale)
post.description:
Signs ONE already-committed sale. Use it when a customer asks for a KRA invoice after the fact; the POS route's `requestEtims` flag does the same thing at the till.

**POST-COMMIT, ALWAYS.** The sale is already final — this can never alter its stock, its ledger entries or its totals, and it posts NOTHING to the ledger: the VAT was posted at sale time, and a fiscal invoice is an attestation, not a financial event. The only field it changes on the sale is `fiscalStatus`.

**The three outcomes, which are deliberately distinct:**
* **SIGNED** — KRA signed it. The receipt number, signature and QR are fiscal fact and are now immutable.
* **REJECTED** (`fiscalStatus` FAILED) — KRA was REACHABLE and refused the payload. **Never auto-retried**: retrying what KRA already refused just refuses again. Fix the cause and use `/invoices/:id/retry`.
* **QUEUED** (`fiscalStatus` PENDING_ETIMS) — KRA was UNREACHABLE. The invoice KEEPS its allocated number and is retried later. Reallocating a number would file the sale with KRA twice.

**Idempotent:** a sale that already has a SIGNED invoice returns it untouched. A sale is filed once.

**400** if the tenant has no active eTIMS credentials, if the device is not initialized, or if the sale is VOIDED (a sale that did not happen must not be declared).

parameters.name: saleId
parameters.description: The sale to file with KRA.

post.summary: File the credit note that reverses a SIGNED sale
post.description:
The fiscal reversal of a sale KRA has already accepted, referencing the original invoice — KRA requires a credit note to come from the same solution that filed the sale.

Voiding a signed sale RECORDS this obligation automatically and atomically with the void (see `POST /v1/pos/sales/:id/void`), because a refund must never wait on KRA being reachable. This route is what DISCHARGES it, and it may also be called directly.

**409** unless the original sale invoice is SIGNED: there is nothing to reverse if KRA never accepted the sale, and an unsigned invoice is corrected by fixing and resubmitting it instead.

A credit note never downgrades the sale's `fiscalStatus`: the sale IS signed, permanently. The reversal is its own fiscal record.

reason.description: Why the sale is being reversed. KRA records it, and a credit note without a reason is unfileable.

parameters.name: saleId
parameters.description: The sale to file with KRA.

get.summary: List fiscal invoices (the operator's dashboard)
get.description:
Newest first. **This is the failed-invoice dashboard**, and the two failure filters mean different things and need different actions:

* `?status=REJECTED` — KRA was reachable and refused these. Each carries KRA's own `resultCode` and `resultMsg`. **An operator must fix the cause and resubmit**; nothing retries them automatically, by design.
* `?status=QUEUED` — KRA was unreachable. These are retried automatically (`npm run etims:retry`) with the numbers they already hold, and usually clear themselves.
* `?status=FAILED` — connectivity retries were exhausted. These need an operator too.

Nothing in any of these lists has affected the books: every one of these sales is committed, correct and final, with its VAT already posted. What is outstanding is the attestation to KRA.

get.summary: Get one fiscal invoice
get.description: Includes KRA's artifacts when SIGNED, and KRA's rejection code and message when REJECTED. The submitted payload and raw response are held for audit but are not returned here.

post.summary: Resubmit an unsigned invoice
post.description:
The operator's "I fixed the cause, try again" action behind a REJECTED row, and the manual push behind a QUEUED one. Also how a recorded credit-note obligation is discharged.

**IT KEEPS THE INVOICE'S EXISTING NUMBER.** That is the no-double-file guarantee: if KRA never received the original submission it files now, and if KRA did receive it, KRA rejects the duplicate number and we learn the truth. Taking a fresh number would file the same sale twice under two numbers and overstate the tenant's declared revenue.

**409** if the invoice is already SIGNED — a signed invoice is a permanent fiscal record and cannot be resubmitted. Reverse it with a credit note if it was wrong.

post.summary: Raise a DRAFT purchase order
post.description:
**A DRAFT HAS NO FINANCIAL EFFECT WHATSOEVER** — no journal entry, no stock movement, nothing committed anywhere but the order itself. An intention to buy is not a transaction.

Each line is priced as quantity x unitCost, rounded once through the same primitive the sale path and every receipt use, so a line's value and the receipt's value agree to the cent. One line per product per order, so "how much of this have we received" has a single answer.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

unitCost.description: Cost per unit as a decimal money string. **Its meaning depends on the tenant's VAT status**: the NET cost for a VAT-registered tenant (input VAT is recoverable, so it is not part of the asset's cost), the VAT-INCLUSIVE cost for a non-registered one (the tax is never coming back, so it IS part of what the goods cost). In both cases this is exactly what reaches account 1200 on receipt.

get.summary: List purchase orders
get.description: Newest order number first. Filter by status (`APPROVED` and `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED` together are the orders goods can still be received against) or by supplier.

get.summary: Get one purchase order with its lines and received quantities

patch.description: **409 once the order leaves DRAFT**, and a database trigger refuses it too. Once an order is APPROVED the SUPPLIER HOLDS A COPY: changing our side of a shared agreement without them does not produce an edited order, it produces a discrepancy that surfaces when the invoice disagrees with the PO.

anyOf.description: Calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).

lines.description: Supplied: the line set is REPLACED wholesale. Omitted: lines are left untouched. Replacement rather than merge is deliberate — a partial merge would need a per-line identity the client does not have, and guessing one silently drops a quantity change. A DRAFT has no received quantities to preserve.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

unitCost.description: Cost per unit as a decimal money string. **Its meaning depends on the tenant's VAT status**: the NET cost for a VAT-registered tenant (input VAT is recoverable, so it is not part of the asset's cost), the VAT-INCLUSIVE cost for a non-registered one (the tax is never coming back, so it IS part of what the goods cost). In both cases this is exactly what reaches account 1200 on receipt.

post.summary: Approve a DRAFT purchase order
post.description:
The order is now committed to the supplier and may be received against. **It still posts nothing** — a commitment to buy is not a transaction, and nothing reaches the ledger until goods actually arrive.

Single-step approval. Multi-level approval and budget checks are deferred; when they arrive they add rows and a policy read, not a change to this transition. Who approved it and when are recorded together and are then immutable.

post.summary: Cancel a purchase order that never happened
post.description:
Permitted from DRAFT and APPROVED only.

**409 once anything has been received.** At that point the order DID happen: value has been accrued to 2050 GRNI and the supplier will still invoice it, so cancelling would orphan a liability. Such an order is CLOSED short instead, which says "we are finished with this" without claiming it never occurred.

post.summary: Close a received or partially-received order
post.description: Terminal. The way to finish with an order that was only partly delivered and will not be completed — the receipts that did happen stand, and their GRNI accrual still awaits its supplier bill. An order with nothing received is CANCELLED instead.

post.summary: Receive goods against a purchase order (creates a GRN)
post.description:
**ONE TRANSACTION, ALL OF IT:** the goods receipt, every line's stock movement, the journal entry, each line's received quantity, and the order's new status. Either all of it commits or none of it does.

**THE POSTING.** Goods arrive with a DELIVERY NOTE, not a tax invoice — so there is no invoiced amount for Accounts Payable and nothing to claim input VAT with. The receipt therefore accrues to GRNI:

* `Dr 1200 Inventory` / `Cr 2050 GRNI` — at the NET cost for a VAT-registered tenant, at the VAT-INCLUSIVE cost for a non-registered one.
* **No VAT is recognised here.** It is recognised when the supplier's bill is booked (Task 5.2), which also clears GRNI to Accounts Payable and posts any difference between the PO price and the invoiced price to 5250 Purchase Price Variance.

Stock and valuation go through the same mover every other stock event uses, so weighted-average cost, the location-ownership check and the `stockCount = SUM(per-location quantity)` invariant all apply unchanged.

**409** unless the order is APPROVED or PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. **400** on an over-receipt, naming the line and what it still expects — a database CHECK refuses it too, because receiving more than was ordered would accrue a liability for goods nobody ordered.

receivingLocationId.description: Where the goods land. Omit for the tenant's MAIN pool — the same defaulting the sale path uses for its selling location, so stock always arrives somewhere specific and the location-ownership rules apply from the moment it lands.

receivedAt.description: The date the goods arrived. Defaults to today. The journal entry is dated to it.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

get.summary: The goods receipts of one purchase order
get.description: Every GRN booked against the order, in the order they arrived, each with its lines and postings (Task T-B-PO-GRN-LIST). 404 for an unknown order.

get.summary: Get a goods receipt with its lines and postings
get.description: A GRN is an IMMUTABLE posted fact — the database refuses both UPDATE and DELETE on it. Each line names the stock movement and the journal entry it produced, and `totalAccrued` is what this receipt added to 2050 GRNI.

post.summary: Enter a DRAFT supplier bill
post.description:
**A DRAFT HAS NO GENERAL-LEDGER EFFECT WHATSOEVER** — no journal entry, no GRNI cleared, no billed quantity advanced. A keyed-in invoice that has not been checked against the delivery is data entry, not a liability, which is exactly why DRAFT is a state and not a flag: a mis-keyed invoice is edited or discarded rather than corrected with a reversing entry.

Each line is one of two kinds. A **PO_MATCH** line invoices goods received against a purchase order and will clear 2050 GRNI; its quantity can never exceed what has been received and not yet billed (the three-way match, held by a database CHECK). An **EXPENSE** line charges an account directly for a cost with nothing received against it.

`billNumber` is the SUPPLIER'S reference and is unique per supplier: **409 if that invoice has already been entered**, which is the duplicate-payment guard.

billNumber.description: THE SUPPLIER'S OWN invoice reference, exactly as printed on their document. Unique per supplier — this is the DUPLICATE-PAYMENT GUARD, and a second entry of the same number is refused with 409.

poId.description: The purchase order this invoice matches. Required if any line is PO-matched; omitted for a standalone expense invoice (rent, electricity, a repair) where nothing was ordered or received.

billDate.description: The invoice date. **The journal entry is dated to it**, not to today.

dueDate.description: Omitted derives from the supplier's payment terms where those parse ("Net 30" -> billDate + 30 days) and otherwise equals billDate — due on receipt. The fallback is deliberately the one that ages the invoice immediately rather than hiding it in "current" for a month.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

unitCost.description: Cost per unit as a decimal money string. On a PO-matched line this is the NET unit cost the SUPPLIER INVOICED — which need not be the cost the order agreed; the difference is the purchase price variance. On an expense line, quantity x unitCost is the line's net amount, so a lump sum is quantity "1" with the whole amount here.

vatRate.description: The VAT percentage the supplier charged on this line, as a decimal STRING matching the Decimal(5,2) column. A RATE, NOT MONEY — never send it as a JSON number and never through a money field. Omitted uses the tenant's default rate. **IGNORED for a non-VAT-registered tenant**, which always records 0.00: there is nothing to recover, and the tax the supplier charged is already part of the line's net cost.

purchaseOrderLineId.description: PO_MATCH. The purchase order line this invoices, which must belong to the bill's own order. The line CLEARS 2050 GRNI at the price the receipt accrued and advances the line's billed quantity, which can never exceed what was received.

expenseAccountCode.description: EXPENSE. The account to charge, for a cost with nothing received against it. Must exist and be of class EXPENSE, COST_OF_SALES or ASSET. **1200, 2000, 2050, 1400 and 5250 are refused**: inventory moves only through the inventory service, and the other four are this posting's own control accounts.

get.summary: List supplier bills
get.description: Newest invoice date first. Filter by status, by supplier, or by `overdue=true` — which means past its due date AND still owed, so a PAID or CANCELLED bill is never overdue however old it is.

parameters.name: overdue
parameters.description: True returns only bills past their due date with a balance outstanding.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The day `overdue` is measured against. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Get one supplier bill with its lines, GRNI clearing and price variance
get.description: Each PO-matched line reports what it took out of GRNI and the resulting price variance, so an auditor can see the difference between the price the order agreed and the price the supplier invoiced without recomputing it.

patch.description: **409 once the bill has been posted**, and a database trigger refuses it too. A posted bill's figures ARE a journal entry that exists: editing `total` afterwards would leave account 2000 carrying an amount no document supports. Cancel it while it is unpaid, or correct it with a supplier credit note.

lines.description: Supplied: the line set is REPLACED wholesale. Omitted: lines are untouched. Replacement rather than merge is deliberate — a partial merge needs a per-line identity the client does not have, and guessing one silently drops a quantity change. A DRAFT has cleared no GRNI, so there is nothing to preserve.

quantity.description: Positive quantity as a Decimal(14,3) string. Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

unitCost.description: Cost per unit as a decimal money string. On a PO-matched line this is the NET unit cost the SUPPLIER INVOICED — which need not be the cost the order agreed; the difference is the purchase price variance. On an expense line, quantity x unitCost is the line's net amount, so a lump sum is quantity "1" with the whole amount here.

vatRate.description: The VAT percentage the supplier charged on this line, as a decimal STRING matching the Decimal(5,2) column. A RATE, NOT MONEY — never send it as a JSON number and never through a money field. Omitted uses the tenant's default rate. **IGNORED for a non-VAT-registered tenant**, which always records 0.00: there is nothing to recover, and the tax the supplier charged is already part of the line's net cost.

purchaseOrderLineId.description: PO_MATCH. The purchase order line this invoices, which must belong to the bill's own order. The line CLEARS 2050 GRNI at the price the receipt accrued and advances the line's billed quantity, which can never exceed what was received.

expenseAccountCode.description: EXPENSE. The account to charge, for a cost with nothing received against it. Must exist and be of class EXPENSE, COST_OF_SALES or ASSET. **1200, 2000, 2050, 1400 and 5250 are refused**: inventory moves only through the inventory service, and the other four are this posting's own control accounts.

post.summary: Post a DRAFT bill to the ledger
post.description:
**This is the operation with the financial effect.** In ONE transaction it posts:

```
Dr 2050 GRNI           what the receipts accrued, at the PO price
Dr <expense accounts>  lines with nothing received against them
Dr 1400 VAT Input      the recoverable tax — only now, because a VAT claim needs a tax invoice
Dr/Cr 5250 PPV         invoiced net minus accrued: the price difference
Cr 2000 Accounts Payable   the gross the supplier is owed
```

**The price variance goes to 5250 rather than onto the stock** because the goods may already have been sold: restating their cost would rewrite a margin that has been reported, and in many cases the units no longer exist. Inventory keeps the cost it was received at, and the discrepancy is visible instead of absorbed. **Nothing here touches account 1200 or any stock table.**

A line that fully bills its purchase order line clears the ENTIRE remaining GRNI accrual, so the account reaches exactly zero rather than nearly zero — GRNI was accrued receipt by receipt, each rounded once, and that sum cannot be reproduced by re-rounding a total. The residue lands in 5250, which is where a price difference belongs.

The entry is dated to `billDate`, so **409 if that accounting period is closed.**

post.summary: Cancel a bill that has not been paid
post.description:
From DRAFT there is nothing to undo. From AWAITING_PAYMENT the bill HAS posted, so cancelling it **REVERSES its journal entry** (a new opposite entry, never an edit — a posted entry is immutable) and **gives the billed quantity back**, because the goods are once again received-and-not-invoiced.

**409 once any payment has been allocated.** Money has left the business, so "this invoice never happened" is no longer true, and the correction is a supplier credit note.

reason.description: Why it is being cancelled. Recorded on the reversing journal entry when the bill had already been posted, so the ledger says why the reversal exists.

post.summary: Record a payment to a supplier, allocated against its bills
post.description:
Posts `Dr 2000 Accounts Payable / Cr 1000 | 1020 | 1010` by method, and applies the allocations, in ONE transaction.

**Every shilling must be allocated**, and the allocations must sum to the payment exactly: there is no on-account supplier balance in this build. An under-allocated payment would be cash out with no invoice reduced — Accounts Payable left overstated while the aging report kept chasing a supplier who had been paid. A DEFERRED database constraint enforces the equality at COMMIT, so no caller can bypass it.

An allocation may never exceed a bill's outstanding balance, a DRAFT bill cannot be paid (it has posted nothing), and a fully PAID bill cannot be paid again — that is the duplicate payment this module exists to prevent.

**A payment is an IMMUTABLE posted fact**: the database refuses UPDATE and DELETE on it and on its allocations.

paymentDate.description: The journal entry is dated to this.

method.description: What selects the credit account: CASH -> 1000, BANK -> 1020, MPESA -> 1010. **MPESA RECORDS, IT DOES NOT DISBURSE** — nothing is sent to Safaricom; this is the record of a payment made elsewhere.

amount.description: The amount that left, as a decimal money string. Must be positive.

reference.description: The external reference: an M-Pesa code, a cheque number, a bank transfer ref.

amount.description: Non-negative KES amount as a decimal string with at most 2 decimal places. Stored as integer minor units (cents). Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

allocations.description: Which invoices this payment settles. **The amounts MUST sum to the payment exactly** — there is no on-account supplier balance in this build, so every shilling is pointed at an invoice. An unallocated remainder would leave Accounts Payable overstated while the aging report kept chasing a supplier who had been paid. The service refuses a mismatch and a DEFERRED database constraint refuses it at COMMIT.

get.summary: List supplier payments with their allocations
get.description: Newest payment number first. Filter by supplier.

get.summary: Get one supplier payment
Accounts payable aging, bucketed by due date, per supplier
get.description:
Buckets: current (not yet due), 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days past the DUE date, over the unpaid balance of every posted bill.

It buckets by DUE date rather than invoice date because the question an owner is asking is "what is late", and an invoice on 60-day terms issued 45 days ago is not late.

Only AWAITING_PAYMENT and PARTIALLY_PAID bills appear: a DRAFT posted nothing and is not a liability, a CANCELLED bill has been reversed, and a PAID one is settled. **`grandTotal` is the accounts payable that supplier bills have put into account 2000**, and the two reconciling is the acceptance criterion for this module.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The day ages are measured from. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Supplier statement — every posted invoice and payment with a running balance
get.description:
Date order, invoices before payments within a day (you are charged before you settle, so a same-day pair reads correctly rather than showing a transient negative balance).

DRAFT and CANCELLED bills are excluded: a cancelled bill's entry has been REVERSED, so showing the charge without the reversal would make the closing balance disagree with account 2000 — and the whole value of a statement is that it reconciles. `closingBalance` equals this supplier's slice of the aging report.

get.summary: Open credit sales — what each customer still owes, oldest first
get.description:
The worklist a receipt is allocated against. Each row's `outstanding` is `SUM(the sale's CREDIT tenders) - arReceived`.

**THE RECEIVABLE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED.** Sale tenders are write-once, so totalling them cannot go stale, and there is deliberately no second column that could disagree with the tenders it claims to total.

Only COMPLETED sales appear: a VOIDED sale's receivable was reversed. Because a sale that has been collected against cannot be voided, those two rules close the loop from both ends — you cannot void a collected sale, and you cannot collect a voided one.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The day `daysOutstanding` is measured to. Defaults to today.

totalOutstanding.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

post.summary: Record a receipt from a customer, allocated against their credit sales
post.description:
Posts, in ONE transaction:

```
Dr 1000 Cash | 1020 Bank | 1010 M-Pesa Till    the money that arrived
Cr 1100 Accounts Receivable                    the debt it settles
```

and in the same transaction raises each allocated sale's `arReceived` and lowers the customer's `creditBalance` by the receipt amount.

**NOTHING ABOUT REVENUE IS TOUCHED.** The sale recognised its income and its output VAT at the till; a receipt that posted to either would recognise the same sale's revenue twice and declare the same tax twice to KRA. This is one asset becoming another.

**Every shilling must be allocated**, and the allocations must sum to the receipt exactly: there is no on-account customer balance in this build. An allocation may never exceed a sale's outstanding credit, a sale with no CREDIT tender cannot be allocated to (it was settled at the till), and a fully settled sale cannot be collected against again.

**A receipt is an IMMUTABLE posted fact**: the database refuses UPDATE and DELETE on it and on its allocations. One consequence worth knowing: once a sale has received money it can no longer be VOIDED, because the void would reverse the receivable while the receipt that settled it stood.

customerId.description: REQUIRED, unlike a sale's customer. Money received against a receivable is by definition received from the person who owes it; an unattributed receipt could not reduce anybody's balance and would put the customer subledger out of step with GL 1100.

receiptDate.description: The date the money arrived. **The journal entry is dated to it**, not to today.

method.description: What selects the debit account: CASH -> 1000, BANK -> 1020, MPESA -> 1010. **MPESA RECORDS, IT DOES NOT COLLECT** — nothing is requested from Safaricom; this is the record of a payment the customer already made.

amount.description: The amount that arrived, as a decimal money string. Must be positive.

reference.description: The external reference: an M-Pesa code, a cheque number, a bank transfer ref.

amount.description: Non-negative KES amount as a decimal string with at most 2 decimal places. Stored as integer minor units (cents). Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

allocations.description: Which credit sales this receipt settles — use `GET /v1/receivables/open` to find them. **The amounts MUST sum to the receipt exactly**: there is no on-account customer balance in this build, so every shilling is pointed at a sale. An unallocated remainder would leave the customer's balance overstated while the aging report kept chasing someone who has paid. The service refuses a mismatch and DEFERRED database constraints — bound to BOTH the receipt and its allocations — refuse it at COMMIT.

get.summary: List customer receipts with their allocations
get.description: Newest receipt number first. Filter by customer, method or date range.

totalReceived.description: Money as a string of integer minor units (KES cents). 125000 means KES 1,250.00. Never a JSON number: 2^53 and float coercion are both real hazards for an accounting API.

get.summary: Get one customer receipt with its allocations
get.description: Includes the journal entry that posted it, derived from the entry's own sourceId rather than stored, so there is no second copy of the link to fall out of step.

get.summary: Accounts receivable aging, bucketed by sale date, per customer
get.description:
Buckets: current (raised today), 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days, over each open credit sale's outstanding amount.

**AGED BY SALE DATE RATHER THAN A DUE DATE**, and that is a scope decision rather than an oversight: `Customer` carries no payment terms, so there is no due date to age from and inventing one would bake a guess into live data. An offline sale ages from its `businessTimestamp` — when the customer actually took the goods — not from when it synced.

Built from the SAME derivation as `GET /open`, so the report and the allocation worklist can never disagree about what is owed. Each row carries the customer's own `creditBalance` column beside its `total`: **the two are equal**, and that is the subledger invariant this module is accountable for.

`grandTotal` equals `SUM(Customer.creditBalance)`, and both equal `GL(1100)` **minus the M-Pesa-failure residual** — the receivable a failed or timed-out STK Push posted to 1100 with no customer attribution (Task 3.3). That residual is reported separately rather than plumbed into the subledger, because re-plumbing it would change a settled guarantee.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The day ages are measured to. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Customer statement — credit sales and receipts with a running balance
get.description:
Date order, sales before receipts within a day (the debt is incurred before it is settled, so a same-day pair reads correctly rather than showing a transient negative balance).

**Only the CREDIT PORTION of each sale appears**, never the sale total: a sale paid half in cash put only the credit half on the customer's account, and charging the whole thing would make the closing balance disagree with `creditBalance`.

VOIDED sales are excluded — the void reversed both the receivable and the balance, so showing the charge without the reversal would break the tie-up, and a statement that does not reconcile is worth nothing. `closingBalance` equals `creditBalance` and this customer's slice of the aging report.

get.summary: Read the effective-dated statutory rulesets, newest first
get.description:
**THERE IS NO ROUTE THAT WRITES A RATE, and that is deliberate.** A statutory figure is the law of Kenya rather than tenant configuration: every MSME on this platform must compute a given month on the SAME bands, or two businesses file different PAYE for the same salary. So the ruleset arrives by the same platform-run seed mechanism as the chart of accounts — provisioning for a new tenant, the migration runner for existing ones — and a statutory update is ONE dated operation across all of them.

Each row carries its `source` and `verifiedOn`, because the engineering ledger makes verifying the in-force figures against an authoritative source and recording the citation a standing requirement rather than a courtesy.

EXACTLY ONE schedule may cover any date — a GiST exclusion constraint over the half-open effective window guarantees it — and a payroll period with no covering schedule REFUSES the run rather than falling back to a later ruleset.

post.summary: Add an employee to the payroll
post.description: Monthly salaried terms: a basic salary plus fixed recurring allowances. A payroll run SNAPSHOTS these into its payslips, so a later revision affects the NEXT run and never a payslip already computed.

kraPin.description: Nullable because an MSME often hires before the number is in hand, and refusing the record would push the employee off the books entirely. Filing (Task 8.2) is where its absence becomes an error.

get.summary: Get one employee with their allowances

patch.description: **IT CHANGES NO PAYSLIP, EVER.** A run snapshots the terms, so a salary revision affects the NEXT run; a DRAFT run only picks it up when explicitly recomputed, and a posted payslip is frozen by a database trigger regardless. That is what makes "what was this employee paid in March" answerable in December.

basicSalary.description: Non-negative KES amount as a decimal string with at most 2 decimal places. Stored as integer minor units (cents). Never send a JSON number — it is rejected.

allowances.description: Supplied: the allowance set is REPLACED wholesale. Omitted: allowances are untouched. Replacement rather than merge is deliberate — a partial merge needs a per-line identity the client does not have, and guessing one silently drops a change.

taxable.description: Defaults to true. A non-taxable allowance is still part of GROSS — and therefore of NSSF, SHIF and the housing levy, which are not income taxes — but is excluded from the pay PAYE is computed on.

patch.summary: Suspend, terminate or reinstate an employee
patch.description: SUSPENDED and TERMINATED both drop the employee out of NEW payroll runs; neither deletes anything. An employee with payroll history can never be deleted, which is why this is a status change — the history is what a P9 is built from. A termination REQUIRES its date, enforced here and by a database CHECK.

status.description: SUSPENDED and TERMINATED both drop the employee out of NEW runs. Neither deletes anything and neither touches a payslip already computed — an employee with payroll history can never be deleted, because the history is what a P9 is built from.

terminationDate.description: REQUIRED when terminating, and refused otherwise: an employee who has left without a leaving date cannot be filed for.

post.summary: Create a DRAFT payroll run for a period and compute its payslips
post.description:
**A DRAFT POSTS NOTHING TO THE LEDGER.** It resolves the statutory schedule governing the period, snapshots every ACTIVE employee's basic pay and allowances, and runs the gross-to-net engine over them. Nothing is committed to the books, which is why the payroll officer can recompute it as often as they like while chasing a missing allowance.

The period must be covered by EXACTLY ONE statutory schedule or the run is **refused**: computing February on March's bands would be invisible in the output, which is precisely what the effective-dated ruleset exists to prevent.

**409 if a non-CANCELLED run already covers the month.** Two live payrolls for one month would double the salary expense, double what every statutory head is owed, and create two net-pay obligations for the same work.

payDate.description: When the net pay is intended to reach employees. **The accrual entry is dated to it.**

get.summary: List payroll runs with their totals
get.description: Newest run number first. Filter by status or period year.

get.summary: Get one payroll run with every payslip
get.description: Each payslip carries every intermediate figure — gross, taxable gross, each statutory contribution, taxable pay, PAYE before and after relief, and net — so it is defensible to the employee and to KRA without re-running the engine.

post.summary: Recompute a DRAFT run against the current employee master
post.description: Replaces every payslip. **409 once the run leaves DRAFT**, and a database trigger refuses it too: a posted run's payslips ARE its accrual entry, so recomputing them would make the seven posted legs disagree with the columns they were summed from.

post.summary: Approve a DRAFT run (owner or manager)
post.description: Freezes the payslips and the schedule the run used, without posting anything. Approval is a separate step from posting because it is where a person signs off the figures, and from that moment they must stop moving.

post.summary: Post the accrual for an APPROVED run (owner or manager)
post.description:
**This is the operation with the financial effect.** In ONE transaction it posts:

```
Dr 6020 Salaries & Wages                  Σ gross pay
Dr 6025 Employer Statutory Contributions  Σ (employer NSSF + employer housing levy)
Cr 2200 PAYE Payable                      Σ PAYE
Cr 2210 NSSF Payable                      Σ (employee + employer NSSF)
Cr 2220 SHA Payable                       Σ SHIF
Cr 2230 Housing Levy Payable              Σ (employee + employer levy)
Cr 2120 Net Salaries Payable              Σ net pay
```

**The employee's own deductions are NOT an expense.** They are already inside the gross in 6020 — the business's cost is what the employee EARNED, and PAYE, NSSF, SHIF and the levy are that same money redirected to the authorities instead of to the employee. Only the EMPLOYER's matched contributions are an additional cost, which is why 6025 carries exactly those two. Debiting the employee's deductions as well would double-count the whole payroll.

The entry is dated to `payDate`, so **409 if that accounting period is closed**. It is asserted to balance before posting and fails loudly otherwise. **Nothing here touches account 1200, any revenue account, or any stock table.**

Paying the net pay out of 2120 is `POST /runs/{id}/settle-net` and remitting the four liabilities is `POST /remittances` (Task 8.2).

post.summary: Cancel a run that has not been posted
post.description:
**409 once the run is POSTED or PAID.** The accrual is booked, every employee has a net-pay claim and three authorities are owed — "this payroll never happened" is false, and the correction is a reversing entry.

Cancelling frees the month: the one-live-run-per-month index excludes CANCELLED runs, so a corrected payroll can be created for the same period.

reason.description: Recorded on the run's notes, so a cancelled payroll says why.

get.summary: The payslips of one run
One payslip, with the earnings it was computed from
get.description: The earnings are a COPY of the employee's terms as they stood when the run was computed, not a reference to the live record — so a later salary revision can never restate what this payslip says the employee was paid.

post.summary: Settle a POSTED run's net pay (owner or manager)
post.description:
In ONE transaction it posts

```
Dr 2120 Net Salaries Payable   Σ the run's payslip net pay
Cr 1000 | 1020 | 1010          by method
```

writes the settlement with ONE audit line per payslip (each employee's own payment method, bank and account SNAPSHOTTED for the bank file a later task builds), and moves the run **POSTED -> PAID**.

**The total is derived from the run's frozen payslips, never accepted from the client**, so the settlement pays exactly what was accrued and GL(2120) for the run returns to exactly zero. A deferred database constraint pins it to the payslips, the lines and the 2120 debit at COMMIT.

**409** if the run is not POSTED, or has already been settled — one net settlement per run, because a second would pay every employee twice. **404** for a run that is not in your tenant. Nothing here touches stock, 1200, revenue or any expense account.

paymentDate.description: The date the money left. **The settlement entry is dated to it**, so 409 if that period is closed.

method.description: The ONE account the whole run is paid from: CASH -> 1000, BANK -> 1020, MPESA -> 1010. MPESA records a payment made over M-Pesa; it disburses nothing.

get.summary: The net-pay settlement of one run, with its per-employee lines
get.description: 404 if the run is unknown or has not been settled yet.

post.summary: Remit one statutory head to its authority (owner or manager)
post.description:
Posts ONE balanced two-leg entry:

```
Dr 2200 PAYE | 2210 NSSF | 2220 SHA | 2230 Housing Levy   by statutoryType
Cr 1000 | 1020 | 1010                                      by method
```

**400 if it would remit more than is owed** — more than the head's current GL credit balance, or (when tagged to a run) more than that run's accrual credited to the head less what is already remitted against it. Both are re-checked by a deferred database constraint at COMMIT. **404** for a run outside your tenant; **409** if the tagged run has not been posted, or the remittance date falls in a closed period.

MPESA records a payment made over M-Pesa; it disburses nothing. A remittance is IMMUTABLE once written.

amount.description: Decimal money string; must be positive. **It may not exceed what is owed**: the head's current GL credit balance, and — when payrollRunId is given — what that run's accrual credited to the head less what has already been remitted against it.

remittanceDate.description: The date the money left. The remittance entry is dated to it.

reference.description: The authority's own payment reference (KRA PRN, NSSF or SHA receipt).

get.summary: Read this tenant's business profile
get.description:
The per-tenant business-configuration singleton: exactly one row per tenant, pinned by a database CHECK so a second is unrepresentable.

It is also the home for the statutory flags payroll and reporting will extend, so that a regime-dependent figure is always read from one place rather than copied.

put.summary: Set the tax regime, KRA PIN and receipt identity (owner only)
put.description:
Omitted fields are left unchanged; null clears an optional field. The receipt fields (legalName, addressLine, phone, email, receiptFooter, showLogoOnReceipt) are what every receipt prints.

**THE REGIME IS MIRRORED.** `taxRegime` here is AUTHORITATIVE (posting reads it). The platform registry's copy of this tenant's regime is updated in the SAME transaction, so the two never disagree; nothing posts from the registry copy.

**CHANGING `taxRegime` CHANGES HOW EVERY FUTURE PURCHASE RECEIPT POSTS.** A VAT-registered business capitalises the net cost of stock and recovers the input VAT; a non-registered one capitalises the VAT-inclusive cost because that tax is unrecoverable. Both are correct for their regime, and which one applies is this setting.

**IT IS NOT RETROACTIVE, deliberately.** It applies to receipts posted from this moment on; stock already received keeps the cost it was received at. Restating the cost of inventory that has already been sold and reported would rewrite settled financial records — a genuinely mis-stated past is corrected with an adjusting entry, never with a silent re-posting.

`isVatRegistered` is derived from `taxRegime` and is not settable: a database CHECK guarantees the two can never disagree, because a business wrongly marked registered would recover VAT it is not entitled to and under-declare to KRA.

taxRegime.description: The tenant's tax regime. **This is what decides how a purchase receipt posts**: VAT_REGISTERED capitalises the NET cost and recovers input VAT, while TURNOVER_TAX and EXEMPT capitalise the VAT-INCLUSIVE cost because that tax is never coming back. `isVatRegistered` is DERIVED from this and cannot be set independently — a database CHECK guarantees the two can never disagree.

kraPin.description: The business's own KRA PIN as printed on its invoices. Public business identity — not the eTIMS integration credential, which is a secret held in the encrypted store.

post.summary: Supersede the statutory schedule from a future commencement date (owner only)
post.description:
Creates a NEW version — a COMPLETE ruleset; prefill from `/current` and override what the law changed — effective from `effectiveFrom`, and in the SAME transaction closes the version in force at that date (its last day becomes the day before). **Forward-only**: refused with 409 if `effectiveFrom` is not after the start of the version in force, after the latest transaction already posted under it, and after the period start of any payroll run computed under it. Nothing already posted is recomputed — every sale, bill and payslip keeps the rates that governed it.

400 on a blank citation, a missing verification date, an out-of-range rate (0–100%; VAT and TOT must be > 0) or a PAYE ladder that is not a contiguous partition from 0 with one open top. Money and rates are decimal strings; a JSON number is rejected.

effectiveFrom.description: The first business day the new version governs. Must be AFTER the start of the version in force AND after the latest transaction already posted under it (and after the period start of any payroll run computed under it): versions are superseded FORWARD only, so no posted transaction ever changes which rates governed it. The version in force is closed at this date.

post.summary: Reconcile M-Pesa pushes whose callback is late

Running it again, or racing a late callback, never posts twice.

post.summary: Safaricom Daraja STK callback (public)
post.description:
**Called by Safaricom, not by clients. The only unauthenticated write path in the system.**

The URL is server-generated: `:pathSecret` is an unguessable secret and `:tenantSlug` is the registered tenant subdomain. Tenant identity is resolved from the PATH — never from the body, which is untrusted input. A wrong secret returns 404 (not 401) so the endpoint is not revealed.

Idempotent: a replayed or duplicate callback for a checkoutRequestId already in a terminal state is a 200 no-op with no second ledger entry. Returns 200 for any well-formed processed callback (providers retry on non-200) and 400 only for a malformed payload.

200.description: Processed, including idempotent no-ops. `status` is one of "confirmed", "failed", "already_processed" or "ignored". A replayed callback returns "already_processed" and has no ledger effect.

schema.description: Processed, including idempotent no-ops. `status` is one of "confirmed", "failed", "already_processed" or "ignored". A replayed callback returns "already_processed" and has no ledger effect.

400.description: Malformed or inauthentic payload; no side effect.

schema.description: Malformed or inauthentic payload; no side effect.

404.description: Wrong path secret or unknown tenant. Deliberately 404 and not 401, so the endpoint is not revealed.

schema.description: Wrong path secret or unknown tenant. Deliberately 404 and not 401, so the endpoint is not revealed.

post.summary: Deliver a simulated M-Pesa callback (development only)
post.description: Registered ONLY when MPESA_PROVIDER=simulated; it does not exist under the real provider. Builds a byte-compatible Daraja envelope and fires it into the real webhook in-process, so tests drive success/failure deterministically without network.

tags.name: Procurement
tags.description: Purchase orders and goods receipts (Module 4). A receipt accrues what is owed to 2050 GRNI — goods arrive with a delivery note, not a tax invoice — and the supplier bill that clears it to Accounts Payable is under Payables.

tags.name: Payables
tags.description: Supplier bills, payments and AP aging (Module 7). A bill is the INVOICE side of procurement: it clears 2050 GRNI at the price the receipt accrued, recognises recoverable input VAT in 1400 (only now — a VAT claim needs a tax invoice), posts any difference between accrued and invoiced price to 5250 Purchase Price Variance, and credits 2000 Accounts Payable. It never writes a stock table and never touches account 1200: a bill changes what is OWED, not what is HELD.

tags.name: Receivables
tags.description: Customer receipts, allocation, AR aging and statements (Module 6). A CREDIT SALE ALREADY IS the receivable: the till posted Dr 1100 / Cr revenue (+ output VAT) and raised the customer's balance, so there is no invoice to create, no VAT to recognise and no price variance here. This is the money coming BACK: Dr cash|bank|M-Pesa / Cr 1100, allocated against specific credit sales. It touches no revenue account and no stock table.

tags.name: Payroll
tags.description: Employees, the effective-dated Kenyan statutory ruleset, the gross-to-net engine and the monthly payroll accrual (Module 8). **No statutory rate is a constant in code** — PAYE bands, NSSF limits, the SHIF rate and the housing levy all live in a dated `StatutorySchedule` that a run records, so a run for a past period stays correct against the rates in force then. Posting books ONE balanced accrual: gross to 6020, the employer's matched contributions to 6025, each statutory head to its own liability and net pay to 2120. It touches no stock table, never posts to 1200 and never touches revenue. SETTLEMENT (Task 8.2) pays the net out of 2120 and remits each statutory head — liability to cash, nothing else — and the filing routes produce the payslip document, the PAYE (P10 shape) / NSSF / SHIF / Housing Levy schedules and the muster roll, each tied to the payslips and to the ledger.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Per-tenant business configuration: the tax regime and VAT status that decide how a purchase receipt splits cost from recoverable input VAT, and the home for the statutory flags payroll and reporting will extend.

tags.name: eTIMS
tags.description: KRA eTIMS OSCU fiscal signing (Module 9). OPT-IN PER SALE and the minority case: most MSME sales are informal and are validly finalized with no fiscal invoice. Each tenant files under THEIR OWN KRA PIN and OSCU device credentials — Angaza is never the integrator and there is no shared signer. Signing is post-commit and posts nothing to the ledger.

tags.name: Offline
tags.description: Offline devices, custody (lease start/renew/end), the sync ingest endpoint that replays captured sales through the real atomic sale transaction, frozen-allocation state, and the admin write-off (Task OFF.1).

tags.name: Support
tags.description: Support-access grants (M4.5 Wave 1). Outside a grant a platform administrator has no access to a business's data. A grant — created by a SUPER_ADMIN after an MFA step-up — scopes ONE administrator to ONE business for at most 8 hours, VIEW or MODIFY (administrative records only); the owner is notified, every access is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail before data is returned, and revocation ends it at once.

tags.name: Mentorship
tags.description: Mentorship & coaching (Module 14). Engagements are created by an admin, CONSENTED to by the business owner, and ended by any party. A mentor reads a business's figures ONLY through an ACTIVE engagement: the business is resolved from the engagement record — never from the request — every read runs READ ONLY through the Module 13 engine, and every read is logged for the owner to see.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Financial statements and reporting (Module 13): income statement, balance sheet, indirect cash flow, trial balance, VAT return / TOT position, and the control-account reconciliation. READ-ONLY — derived from posted journal lines through the ledger's one balance query, ranged by entryDate (never createdAt), each statement asserting its own identity.
